title.rendered: How to get the Dr Eggman skin in Fortnite

content.rendered:
The iconic Sonic villain, Dr Eggman, has arrived in Fortnite, thanks to an ongoing collab between Epic Games and Sega. For a limited time, fans of the blue speedster can grab skins inspired by the rotund villain and other memorable characters such as Shadow and Knuckles in the Item Shop. On the other hand, the Sonic the Hedgehog skin is on sale as part of Fortnite Override’s Battle Pass, worth 800 V-Bucks, throughout the season.

While Dr Eggman and Knuckles the Echidna skins can be purchased for 1,500 V-Bucks, the Shadow the Hedgehog skin is pricier at 1,800 V-Bucks. These three outfits and related cosmetics are available to buy until August 30, 2026, by 5 PM PT or 8 PM ET.

Steps to claim the Dr Eggman skin in Fortnite

  1. In Fortnite, navigate to the Shop tab.
  2. Next, scroll down to the Sonic the Hedgehog section and select your desired skin.
  3. Finally, press and hold the Purchase button to complete your transaction.

By shelling out V-Bucks for the Dr Eggman skin, you will also get the Orbot and Cubot back bling for free. This item otherwise costs 300 V-Bucks when purchased solo from the in-game store.

All Dr Eggman Bundle items in Fortnite

In addition to the Dr Eggman skin, there is a wide range of cosmetics inspired by Sonic’s nemesis that you can grab by purchasing the Dr Eggman Bundle, priced at 2,000 V-Bucks. While those items are also available for purchase individually in the Item Shop, you save a total of 1,600 V-Bucks by bagging all of them in a single swoop with the bundle purchase.

1. Egg Hammer

Price: 600 V-Bucks
Also available with: Dr Eggman Bundle

2. Orbot and Cubot (back bling)

Price: 300 V-Bucks
Also available with: Dr Eggman skin, Dr Eggman Bundle

3. Egg Mobile (emote)

Price: 500 V-Bucks
Also available with: Dr Eggman Bundle

4. Eggman’s E-TAR (pickaxe and back bling)

Price: 800 V-Bucks
Also available with: Dr Eggman Bundle

Wrapping up

There is no doubt that Dr Eggman’s inclusion in the Fortnite skins catalog brings a memorable video game villain into the mix. While the Sonic the Hedgehog antagonist is only the latest name in a long list of gaming icons who have made their way onto Fortnite, he is arguably among the few major names when we talk about gaming antagonists exclusively.

Besides Dr Eggman, there are a few more villainous video game characters, namely as Adam Smasher, Psycho Bandit, and Huggy Wuggy, that have appeared in Fortnite before, but no one else beyond those four really. Based on the dearth of characters in this category, it will be exciting to see Epic Games bring more villains from popular gaming franchises as part of their future collabs.

FAQs

1. How many Sonic The Hedgehog character skins are available in Fortnite?

At the time of writing, there are four different Sonic franchise characters up for grabs, namely Sonic, Dr Eggman, Knuckles, and Shadow.

2. Can I get the Sonic the Hedgehog skin from the Item Shop?

No, you must purchase the Fortnite Override Battle Pass to get the Sonic skin as it isn’t available in the Shop.

3. Is Tails available in Fortnite?

While Tails is not available in Fortnite as a skin, you can still unlock his sidekick version by purchasing the Battle Pass for Chapter 7 Season 4 and reaching Level 2.

title.rendered: I tried Instagram’s First Draft to auto-edit my Reels: Here’s what happened

content.rendered:
Instagram just launched a new feature called First Draft that can automatically turn your video clips into a Reel. Instead of manually trimming every clip and removing awkward pauses, you can let Instagram create a rough edit for you.

I tried it to see how well it actually works and whether it can save time without taking the creative control out of my hands. Here’s how to create Reels with Instagram First Draft.

What exactly is Instagram’s First Draft, and how does it work?

Instagram’s First Draft is essentially an automatic Reel editing tool built directly into the Instagram app. The concept is quite simple. Give Instagram your footage, and with a single tap, it can trim the clips, remove pauses, and assemble them into a first cut for a Reel.

However, the result isn’t the finished video. The feature is deliberately called a First Draft—a starting point that you can change before publishing. You can continue into Instagram’s full Reel editor, adjust clips, reorder them, add music, text and effects, or undo the automatic edits.

Instagram says the feature is designed to handle the tedious early editing work. It can pull together useful portions of multiple videos, perfect for talking-head videos, day-in-the-life content, and multi-clip montages.

Note: At first glance, First Draft certainly looks like an AI video editing feature. It analyzes footage, decides which portions to keep, and automatically assembles a shorter video. But it’s not an AI feature, according to Instagram spokesperson Nicole Rechtszaid.

How to auto-edit Reels using First Draft

Using First Draft is almost comically straightforward. There are currently two ways to start.

Method 1: Use videos already on your iPhone

  1. Open Instagram and tap the plus sign at the top. Move to the Reels section.
  2. Select one or more video clips from your gallery.
  3. Look for the First Draft option.
  4. Tap it and let Instagram create the initial edit.
  5. Review the automatically edited Reel. Tap Add music to choose a suitable song.
  6. Tap Next to continue.
  7. Add text, effects, or voiceover before publishing. Tap Edit video to open the full editor if you want to make other changes or download the Reel.
  8. Finally, tap Next, write a caption, and share your Reel.

Instagram says the automatically generated edit is reversible, so you aren’t surrendering control over your footage.

Method 2: Record your Reel first

You can also use First Draft immediately after filming.

  1. Go to Instagram, swipe right to open the camera, and move to the Reels section.
  2. Now, tap and hold the shutter to record your clips.
  3. Tap Next, then select First Draft to generate the initial version.
  4. From there, you can review the edit and continue into the normal Reel editor.
  5. Once satisfied, share your reel.

The important thing is not to think of that first result as your finished Reel.

My experience with Instagram’s new editing feature

The biggest benefit of First Draft isn’t that it creates a Reel. It’s that it gets you out of the blank timeline. That’s a much bigger deal than it sounds.

When you’re editing manually, there’s always that annoying first stage where you have to figure out what belongs in the video at all. You watch the same clip, drag the handles, remove the silence, move to the next clip, and repeat.

First Draft attacks exactly that part of the process.

What Instagram got right

The first thing Instagram got right is the friction. There’s virtually no learning curve. You don’t need to understand timelines, cuts, or complicated editing controls to get an initial Reel.

What I like is reversibility. It is important to note that automatic editing may be wrong, as many aspects of video creation are rather subjective. Instagram can decide that a pause is unnecessary; I might think that pause makes the moment feel natural.

Meta also appears to be deliberately positioning the feature as a way to handle technical production while leaving the creative decisions to the creator. That’s also why the feature feels less threatening than some of the more aggressive AI video tools appearing elsewhere.

Where First Draft falls short

Here’s my biggest complaint: automatic trimming is not the same thing as good editing.

Removing a pause can make a talking-head Reel tighter. But sometimes a pause is the shot, or the awkward second is the joke, or the five seconds Instagram thinks are unnecessary are exactly what gives a clip personality.

That’s the fundamental limitation of First Draft. It can make decisions about footage, but a good Reel isn’t simply a collection of the “best” moments. It’s a story, rhythm, context, and when not to cut.

So I wouldn’t hand First Draft a folder of clips and blindly publish whatever comes back. That defeats the point of being a creator. Instead, I’d use it as an aggressive first pass, and then take control again.

First Draft vs. Instagram’s Edits app

This is where I think Instagram has created an interesting problem for itself. Meta already has Edits, its dedicated video-editing app. So why put an automatic Reel editor inside Instagram instead of making it an Edits feature? It’s a fair question.

First Draft currently lives inside Instagram, where the entire process, from filming to editing to publishing, can happen without leaving the app. That’s incredibly convenient for casual creators.

But Edits is meant for serious video creation. It already includes AI video generation tools. So, First Draft would arguably make even more sense there. Interestingly, creators have already questioned why First Draft wasn’t launched in Edits. And Meta said it could make the feature available in both apps if creators wanted it.

But for now, the winner is Instagram in terms of convenience. If I’m already inside Instagram with my clips ready to go, having to open another app just to make a rough cut would be ridiculous. First Draft removes that extra step.

Who should actually use it?

I don’t think First Draft is for everyone.

  • Casual Instagram creators: If you normally avoid making Reels because video editing feels like too much work, this is perfect for you. Simply shoot a handful of clips and get a usable starting point without learning an editing app.
  • People who post frequently: Do you produce several Reels a week? First Draft can handle the repetitive trimming while you spend your time on the hook, story, captions, music, and final pacing.

However, if you already know your way around CapCut, Premiere Pro, Final Cut Pro, or another editor, First Draft isn’t going to suddenly replace your workflow. It may become the rough-cut machine.

Last but not least, creators whose videos have a distinct editing style should use this function with caution. For content that depends heavily on timing, comedic pauses, storytelling, or highly specific pacing, First Draft can accidentally remove what makes your video yours.

Final verdict

After trying Instagram’s First Draft, I think it’s a useful shortcut rather than a complete Reel-making solution. It does a good job of creating a quick starting point, but I’d still want to make the final cuts myself.

If you regularly make Reels and want to spend less time on basic trimming, First Draft is worth trying. Just think of it as your first edit, not your final one.

What do you think about the Instagram First Draft feature? Let me know in the comments below!

title.rendered: Fortnite Chapter 7 Season 4 Override: All map changes explained

content.rendered:
Fortnite Override finally rolled out last Thursday, unfurling a season-long celebration of some of the biggest video game franchises in the world. It not only brought gaming-related cosmetics but also added some brand-new map areas inspired by iconic video game locations and more.

Apart from bringing some visual freshness to the Battle Royale map, these changes introduced in Fortnite Chapter 7 Season 4 also have some gameplay elements unique to them. For instance, while one particular location has launchers that send you sprinting in a flash, the other is a puzzling shape-shifting maze.

In this article, you can check out the entire list of newly added Fortnite Override map changes, along with what makes them stand out from the rest of the island.

New map locations in Fortnite Override

Green Hill Zone

This area in the Battle Royale map is inspired by the namesake location shown in the Sonic the Hedgehog franchise. It houses various aspects that Sonic fans would be familiar with, such as hooped tracks, collectible gold rings, speed boosters, and jump springs. Since some of these influence the gameplay, particularly traversal, they give Fortnite’s Green Hill Zone a unique identity.

Moreover, the venue also has plenty of common chests and sprite chests scattered throughout, making its exploration rewarding for players. Due to such abundance, in each match, you will see many players land in this area. As a result, it’s best to stay alert when in Green Hill Zone. Courtesy of the speed boosters, grind rails, and jump springs, escaping a firefight isn’t a tough ask anyway, if push comes to shove.

Pac-Man islands

There are not one but three different islands in the shape of popular Pac-Man characters. This lineup includes the titular protagonist and two of its enemies, namely Pinky and Blinky. On the one hand, the Pac-Man island is located at the northern tip of the island, between Lifty Lodge and Latte Landing. On the other hand, Blinky and Pinky are located near the western and eastern corners of the map, respectively, on either side of Sunken Shores.

These three islands have a fair number of chests, usually found under the trees, which is why they are frequented by quite a few players. Owing to this, it is imperative to constantly watch your back when you are in this zone, as there is little to no cover to protect you from enemy fire.

Reality’s Reign

Reality’s Reign is a very futuristic-looking place in Fortnite’s new Battle Royale map. The design of its structures is heavily inspired by hardware components that are prevalent in the PC gaming landscape, such as liquid-cooled GPUs.

This is another place that has a sufficient number of chests. However, given that it also provides an ample amount of cover and places to hide, it is relatively safer to land here compared to some of the other locations mentioned previously.

Stone Sanctum

This stone structure in Fortnite Override is reminiscent of the ancient temples often seen in films and similar media. Similar to Reality’s Reign, Stone Sanctum also has a fair number of chests spread across its length and breadth, on top of enough places to take cover or hide from enemies.

What makes exploring this complex and chasing opponents in it trickier is the shape-shifting nature of its walls. Hence, it’s a great place for those looking to lose pursuers but an annoying place for those chasing after other players.

Sunken Shores (Tetris-ified)

Although Sunken Shores is a location inherited from Chapter 7 Season 3, it is worth mentioning in this list because the devs have given it a significant refresh, incorporating heavy Tetris influence. The highly iconic Tetris blocks can now be spotted sprouting out of the decrepit houses. Their color certainly adds a level of vibrance to the otherwise dull-looking flooded area that is the original Sunken Shores.

Rounding up

These new locations added in Fortnite Override have certainly become key points of interest in the game, drawing flocks of players to them throughout a given match. Their unique characteristics, such as shape-shifting mazes, grind rails, and jump springs, make for an intriguing gameplay twist not present in the previous season.

As Fortnite Chapter 7 Season 4 progresses, it will be worth keeping an eye on how the popularity of these key locations changes over time. At the time of writing, it doesn’t seem like players are even remotely tired of landing in these locations in spite of the early elimination risk involved. Whether this remains the case going forward or not is something only time will tell.

Don’t miss these related reads:

  • Fortnite Chapter 7 Season 3: All confirmed skins and collabs
  • Fortnite Festival Season 15: Lil Tecca skin and cosmetics revealed

mainEntity.name: 1. How many Sonic The Hedgehog character skins are available in Fortnite?

acceptedAnswer.text: At the time of writing, there are four different Sonic franchise characters up for grabs, namely Sonic, Dr Eggman, Knuckles, and Shadow.

mainEntity.name: 2. Can I get the Sonic the Hedgehog skin from the Item Shop?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, you must purchase the Fortnite Override Battle Pass to get the Sonic skin as it isn't available in the Shop.

mainEntity.name: 3. Is Tails available in Fortnite?

title.rendered: M6 Mac mini vs M5 Ultra Mac Studio: Which one should you choose?

content.rendered:
Apple has refreshed its Mac desktop lineup with the launch of the new M6 Mac mini and M5 Ultra Mac Studio. Both bring a significant boost in performance, but they target different types of users.

The M6 Mac mini delivers powerful performance in a compact, affordable package, while the M5 Ultra Mac Studio is built for demanding workloads, including video editing, 3D rendering, and AI workloads. So, which one should you buy?

In this M6 Mac mini vs M5 Ultra Mac Studio comparison, we’ll look at their design, performance, specs, connectivity, and pricing to help you decide which Mac is right for you.

M6 Mac mini vs M5 Ultra Mac Studio: Quick comparison

But specifications alone don’t tell you which one belongs on your desk.

M6 Mac mini vs M5 Ultra Mac Studio: What’s the actual difference?

Design, weight, and size

The M6 Mac mini wins this round before the M5 Ultra Mac Studio even gets out of its box.

The Mac mini’s current chassis measures just 12.7 × 12.7 cm (5 × 5 inches). The previous M4 model weighed 0.67kg, and Apple has retained the same ultracompact design for the M6 model. It is the sort of computer you can put beside a monitor and forget about. I can easily move it between desks and build it into a surprisingly clean home-office setup.

The Mac Studio is compact by workstation standards, but it is much larger and heavier. Its chassis measures 19.7 × 19.7 × 9.5 cm, while the M5 Ultra version weighs about 3.6kg. That’s still remarkably small for a machine capable of running hundreds-of-billions-of-parameter AI models locally.

If your priority is minimum desk space, portability, and simplicity, the M6 Mac mini is the obvious winner. However, for sustained workstation performance, the Mac Studio’s larger thermal system is part of the reason it can deliver so much more.

Performance: M6 vs M5 Ultra

This is where the M6 Mac mini vs M5 Ultra Mac Studio performance comparison gets brutal.

The M6 is impressive precisely because it is not a workstation chip. Apple says its 12-core CPU delivers the world’s fastest single-threaded performance and up to 1.2x the multithreaded performance of M5. Its 12-core GPU includes Neural Accelerators, while its Dual 16-core Neural Engine is designed to accelerate on-device AI.

For everyday work, that is more than enough. You can open dozens of browser tabs, run Microsoft Office, edit photos, compile code, run local AI tools, and edit a 4K project. The M6 Mac mini should feel extremely quick.

Then you look at the M5 Ultra. It uses Apple’s first quad-die architecture and scales to 36 CPU cores and 80 GPU cores. It starts with 96GB of unified memory, 1 TB of storage, and 1.2 TB/s of memory bandwidth.

This isn’t simply a faster version of the M6. It is a different class of computer. For complex 3D rendering, visual effects, scientific workloads and demanding local AI, M5 Ultra is the highest-performance desktop chip. Apple says M5 Ultra can provide up to 1.3x the multithreaded performance of M3 Ultra.

My take: don’t buy the M5 Ultra because you want a “fast Mac.” Buy it because you have a workload that can actually consume its horsepower.

Memory and storage

This may be the biggest reason to buy the Mac Studio. The M6 Mac mini supports up to 32GB of unified memory and up to 170GB/s of memory bandwidth. That’s excellent for a compact desktop, but 32GB creates a hard ceiling for users with unusually demanding workloads.

The M5 Ultra Mac Studio goes in the opposite direction. It supports up to 512GB of unified memory and 16 TB of storage. This allows users to work with enormous datasets and run huge LLMs with hundreds of billions of parameters entirely on-device.

That difference matters enormously for M6 Mac mini vs M5 Ultra Mac Studio for AI. For normal AI assistants, image generation, coding tools, and smaller local models, M6 is already surprisingly capable.

But if your goal is to run enormous models locally without relying on cloud GPUs, the M5 Ultra’s memory capacity changes what is possible. This is one of those specifications you may not appreciate today, but could become the reason you buy the Mac Studio five years from now.

Ports and connectivity

The Mac mini is small, but Apple hasn’t made it feel starved for connections. M6 gets Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6 and 2.5Gb Ethernet, with 10Gb Ethernet available as a configuration option. It has two USB-C ports on the front and three Thunderbolt 4 ports on the back, plus HDMI and Ethernet. For an everyday desktop, that’s plenty.

The Mac Studio is much more serious about connectivity. M5 Ultra gets four Thunderbolt 5 ports, two front Thunderbolt 5 ports, an SDXC card slot, two USB-A ports, HDMI, a 10Gb Ethernet connection, and a headphone jack. Thunderbolt 5 supports transfer rates up to 120Gbps and can connect high-speed storage, displays and PCIe expansion hardware.

For professional photographers and filmmakers, the front SDXC slot itself makes the Studio a better choice than most options. Moreover, the greater I/O translates into fewer adapters, converters, and compromises in professional workstations.

Bonus: Both Mac mini and Mac Studio support Genlock over USB-C. So, you can synchronize a display with camera signals during a multi-camera shot.

Noise and power consumption

This is an underrated reason to choose the Mac mini.

The M6 is built around Apple’s 2nm process and is explicitly designed for high performance per watt. It’s best for everything from everyday productivity to always-on AI workloads. The Mac mini’s compact thermal design has also been engineered to keep the machine cool and quiet. Apple claims it’s just 5dBA at idle and a 155W maximum continuous power rating.

The M5 Ultra Mac Studio obviously has a much higher performance ceiling, and its thermal system is built for sustained professional workloads. Mac Studio specifications list a 480W maximum continuous power rating, illustrating the much larger power envelope of the Studio class.

In other words, the Mac mini is the better choice for a machine that quietly sits on your desk all day. The Mac Studio is ideal when you want the computer to spend hours rendering, encoding, simulating, or running AI workloads at full tilt.

Price-to-performance: Which is the better value?

Pricing makes the M6 Mac mini vs M5 Ultra Mac Studio comparison almost ridiculous.

The M6 Mac mini starts at $899. The M5 Ultra Mac Studio starts at $5499. That’s more than six times the starting price of the Mac mini. And no, the M5 Ultra is not six times faster at everything. That’s the important part.

If you spend your day in Chrome, Slack, Word, Excel, Photoshop, Lightroom, coding environments, and occasional video editors, the Mac mini already gives you far more performance than you probably need.

The Studio’s premium becomes rational when its additional CPU cores, GPU resources, memory bandwidth, and enormous memory pool save you meaningful time.

Think about a professional editor who spends hours every week waiting for renders, a 3D artist who needs more memory to load his scenes, or an AI researcher who prefers to use huge models on his machine rather than spend money on GPU hours in the cloud. For those people, the Mac Studio isn’t expensive in the same way a luxury computer is expensive.

It is expensive in the way that productive equipment is expensive. For everyone else, I’d put the money into a better display, faster external storage, backup hardware, and a comfortable desk setup before jumping to M5 Ultra.

Who should buy the M6 Mac mini?

Buy the M6 Mac mini if you want the best Mac desktop to buy in 2026 for most people.

It makes the most sense for:

  • Students and home users
  • Office and productivity users
  • Developers who don’t need massive build environments
  • Photographers
  • Casual and semi-professional video editors
  • Content creators
  • AI enthusiasts experimenting with local models
  • Small businesses
  • Anyone building a compact workstation
  • Buyers who already own a good monitor, keyboard, and mouse

The M6 is particularly compelling because it brings serious AI capability into Apple’s smallest desktop. Its 12-core CPU, 12-core GPU, Neural Accelerators and Dual 16-core Neural Engine give it considerably more headroom for modern AI workloads than the typical “basic Mac” label might suggest.

Without any second thoughts, I would go for the Mac mini for daily use. However, when talking about creators, the answer may not be that straightforward. If you primarily edit photos, 4K video, and social content, you should start with the Mac mini and move upward only when you can identify a specific limitation.

Who should buy the M5 Ultra Mac Studio?

The M5 Ultra Mac Studio is for a very specific kind of buyer.

You should consider it if you’re a:

  • Professional filmmaker
  • VFX artist
  • 3D designer or animator
  • High-end video editor
  • AI researcher
  • Machine-learning developer
  • Data scientist
  • Scientific researcher
  • Developer working with extremely large projects or datasets
  • Professional who regularly runs sustained CPU/GPU workloads

For video editing, the Studio is the clear choice once your workflow involves serious 8K production, complex effects, high-resolution timelines or multiple demanding streams. Apple says M5 Ultra’s Media Engine can handle up to 33 simultaneous streams of 8K ProRes 422 at 30fps.

Final verdict

So, which Mac should you choose: Mac mini or Mac Studio?

Here’s the simple answer.

  • Buy the M6 Mac mini if you’re asking whether you need the Mac Studio.
  • Buy the M5 Ultra Mac Studio if you already know exactly why you need it.

The M6 Mac mini is the smarter choice for almost everyone. At $899, it delivers a remarkable combination of CPU performance, graphics, AI acceleration, compact design and power efficiency.

The M5 Ultra Mac Studio is the specialist weapon. Its up-to-36-core CPU, 80-core GPU, 512GB memory capacity, and 1.2TB/s bandwidth are built for workloads that would make an ordinary desktop sweat.

So don’t let the M5 Ultra’s enormous specifications seduce you into spending $5499 when you don’t need them.

title.rendered: This fan-made iPhone Ultra teaser looks almost like an Apple launch video

content.rendered:
Designer Gunho Lee has released a 65-second fan-made concept video imagining how Apple could introduce its rumored foldable iPhone. It is not an Apple ad, a leak, or an official product preview. The design, specs, and even the iPhone Ultra name remain unconfirmed.

It turns foldable rumors into something you can picture using

The clip follows an actor through a normal day. He pulls a short, wide iPhone from his pocket, opens it like a book, unlocks it with Touch ID, watches a movie, runs two apps side by side, and takes a call. An exploded product shot then shows the hinge, two battery cells, and an A20 Pro chip.

Those choices line up with months of rumors, including the passport-like proportions seen in an earlier iPhone Ultra dummy unit and reports that Apple’s foldable could use Touch ID in the side button. Lee packages those ideas with Apple’s familiar slow camera moves and carefully lit product close-ups.

The best part is how quickly the odd shape starts to look normal. Seeing the device come out of a pocket and open into a wider screen explains the appeal better than another CAD image. The outer display never gets a clear hero shot, even though the hinge and inner hardware receive plenty of attention.

Apple has an event, but no foldable announcement yet

Apple has scheduled a special event for September 9 at 10 a.m. PT. The company has not said which products it will announce, so the foldable iPhone and its rumored iPhone Ultra name are still unofficial.

Even if Apple shows the device, it may not go on sale with the iPhone 18 Pro models. Analyst Ming-Chi Kuo expects an iPhone X-style launch, with the announcement followed by a later pre-order window because of limited early production.

That leaves less than two weeks to see whether Apple’s real presentation looks anything like Lee’s version. Until then, every feature in this polished teaser is still an artist’s interpretation of the rumors.

mainEntity.name: 1. How many Sonic The Hedgehog character skins are available in Fortnite?

acceptedAnswer.text: At the time of writing, there are four different Sonic franchise characters up for grabs, namely Sonic, Dr Eggman, Knuckles, and Shadow.

mainEntity.name: 2. Can I get the Sonic the Hedgehog skin from the Item Shop?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, you must purchase the Fortnite Override Battle Pass to get the Sonic skin as it isn't available in the Shop.

mainEntity.name: 3. Is Tails available in Fortnite?

acceptedAnswer.text: While Tails is not available in Fortnite as a skin, you can still unlock his sidekick version by purchasing the Battle Pass for Chapter 7 Season 4 and reaching Level 2.

title.rendered: Apple’s September 9 event is official, with iPhone 18 Pro and foldable expected

content.rendered:
Apple has announced a special event for Wednesday, September 9, at 10:30 PM IST. The official Apple Events page calls it “Surprise and shine” and says the stream will be available on Apple.com and in the Apple TV app.

The invitation shows a glowing blue-and-pink Apple logo with a bright flare at its center. Apple has not explained the artwork, and it has not named a single product for the event.

The iPhone 18 Pro and foldable remain expected, not confirmed

The leading expectation is a smaller iPhone lineup than Apple usually brings to September. Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman has reported that Apple plans to show the iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, and its first foldable iPhone.

That lines up with identifiers found in iOS 27 beta code, which are believed to map to the two Pro models and a foldable for fall 2026. The foldable is reportedly called “iPhone Ultra” inside Apple, but its final name is still unknown.

In a separate report, Gurman said people who have used the foldable like its pocketable design, hinge, and larger-screen software. The reported early impressions add weight to the rumor, but Apple has confirmed none of the device’s design, cameras, price, or release details.

A standard iPhone 18 is not expected at this event. Apple is reportedly preparing to split the iPhone 18 generation into two launches, with the regular iPhone 18, iPhone 18e, and iPhone Air 2 following in spring 2027.

Gurman’s expected event list also includes Apple Watch Series 12, Apple Watch Ultra 4, a new Apple TV 4K, HomePod mini 2, and a possible preview of Apple’s long-rumored home hub. Apple could change that lineup, and its invitation confirms none of it.

How to watch Apple’s September event

The event starts at 10:30 PM IST on September 9. Apple will stream it on its Events website, through the Apple TV app, and on YouTube Live. The official calendar entry blocks out two hours, though the presentation may finish earlier.

Apple has locked the date, time, and stream. The foldable stays in the rumor column until it appears on stage.

title.rendered: iPhone 17 was the world’s best-selling smartphone again in Q2 2026

content.rendered:
Apple’s base iPhone 17 remained the world’s best-selling smartphone in the second quarter of 2026. A new Counterpoint Research report estimates that it accounted for 6% of global smartphone unit sales, ahead of the iPhone 17 Pro Max and iPhone 17 Pro.

That is the second straight quarter with the same Apple trio in the top three. The iPhone 17 also led Q1 with a 6% share.

Apple and Samsung took every top-10 spot

Apple placed five phones in the Q2 ranking. The iPhone 17e finished seventh, while the older iPhone 16 came tenth. Samsung filled the other five places, led by the Galaxy S26 Ultra in fourth.

The S26 Ultra was the quarter’s best-selling Android phone. Counterpoint says this is the first time an ultra-premium Android model has led Android sales in a June quarter. Samsung’s Galaxy A07 4G, two versions of the Galaxy A17, and the base Galaxy S26 completed the list.

Together, the ten models made up 26% of all smartphone unit sales, compared with 24% a year earlier. Counterpoint links that concentration to phone makers focusing on flagship and high-volume models as the memory shortage raises costs.

The base iPhone is doing the heavy lifting

Counterpoint credits the base iPhone 17’s upgrades with closing some of the gap with Apple’s Pro models. Apple’s total unit sales rose 5% year over year, with gains in India, Japan, the Middle East, and Africa. Sales nearly doubled in South Korea.

The Pro models still benefited from trade-ins, promotions, and financing. The iPhone 17e made the top 10 after Apple added MagSafe and more base storage without raising its starting price from the previous model.

The iPhone-heavy ranking reflects a broader move toward premium phones. A separate Counterpoint report estimates that Apple held 65% of premium smartphone unit sales in the first half of 2026, even as the wider market weakened.

Global smartphone shipments fell 11% year over year in Q2, according to separate Counterpoint data. Samsung led total brand shipments with 24%, while Apple reached a record 20% Q2 share. That does not conflict with the iPhone 17 ranking. Samsung sells more phones overall across a much broader lineup, while Apple’s base flagship was the single most popular model.

content.rendered:
Update: Verified the latest Military Tycoon codes on August 27, 2026

Military Tycoon makes you pay for every serious base upgrade, vehicle, and push across the map. Free Cash speeds up the build, while Diamonds, Season Points, boosts, and crates unlock rewards that take longer to grind. The codes below give you all five without spending Robux. Redeem them before expanding your base because older Military Tycoon codes rotate out with little warning.

All working Military Tycoon codes

  • wewantmore: 1 Daily Crate (New)
  • b21raider: 1 Daily Crate (New)
  • loadsofdiamonds: 50 Diamonds
  • heatofthemoment: 500 Season Points
  • summertime: 2-hour Cash boost
  • warfund: 100,000 Cash
  • betterperformance: 50 Diamonds
  • frontlines: 1 Soldier Card Pack
  • seasonrush: 1,000 Season Points
  • nukenation: 1-hour Cash boost

Expired and disputed Military Tycoon codes

bugfixesyay, seasonpush, limitedcommunitycode, f16falcon, nukebase, noupdate, 1mlikes, thereturn, 500mvisits, fixes, newjet, happysaturday, 900klikes, LT01, PL01, t90, 10k, patch22, terbyte, terabyte, 1day, 2days, 3days, 4days, freecash, skins, weekday, goldcar, 780k, 100mvis, flyingfortress, 1mmembers, 90mvis, 250klikes, 500kfavs, 80mvis, CREDITS, 200klikes, Halloween, military2022!, 70mvis, WorldWar, ARTILLERY, Hooray50k, ghostship, bugs, followers5k, 600klikes, 550klikes, newplane, f16, hollidayu, lagfixed, heist, 450klikes, 400klikes, badegghunt, Outage, 24ktank, battlecruiser, missiletruck, 300klikes, 110mvis, island, ilovebugs, battleship.

How to redeem Military Tycoon codes

Military Tycoon hides its code box behind the thumbs-up button. Wait for your base to load before opening it.

  1. Open Military Tycoon on Roblox.
  2. Press the thumbs-up button at the top-right.
  3. Paste a working code into the text box.
  4. Press Redeem to collect the reward.

Why your Military Tycoon code is not working

Run through these quick checks before testing a long-expired list:

  • The code expired: Update, event, and milestone codes can disappear without warning.
  • You already used it: Most Military Tycoon codes work once per Roblox account.
  • The spelling is wrong: The current codes are lowercase and may be case-sensitive. Copy and paste them.
  • Your server is old: Rejoin the experience once when a newly released code fails.
  • The code is disputed: Several older trackers still call dead strings active, so use the 10-code list above first.

If a code fails again in a fresh server, move on. Retyping it will not revive an expired reward.

Where to find more Military Tycoon codes

New codes tend to arrive with updates, seasonal events, visit milestones, or bug fixes. Watch Military Tycoon on X, join the official Discord, and check the InfinityInteractive Roblox community after a new update.

Bookmark this page if you would rather skip the announcement hunt and test only the short list. For another base-building grind, try the latest Doors codes, Evade codes or browse the complete list of all Roblox game codes for more free rewards.

title.rendered: How to Add Your Driver’s License or State ID to Apple Wallet

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Benefits of Digital IDs in Apple Wallet: Digital IDs simplify travel and identity checks with faster TSA screening, stronger privacy, device-level encryption, and broad compatibility across supported iPhones.
  • Requirements & Availability for Digital IDs: You’ll need an iPhone 8 or newer running iOS 16.5+, Face or Touch ID, a verified Apple ID, and state support to set up a digital ID.
  • Supported States and Regions: As of 2026, Arkansas, Arizona, Maryland, Colorado, and 10 other states support Apple Wallet IDs, with more states and the UK preparing wider adoption soon.
  • How to Add Your Digital ID to Apple Wallet: Setup requires opening Wallet, selecting your state, scanning your physical ID, and completing Apple’s secure verification process directly on your iPhone.
  • Using and Managing Your Digital ID: You can show your ID at TSA, share it with apps, transfer it to new devices, or remove it if you move or no longer need it.

Carrying your physical driver’s license or state ID everywhere can be a hassle and risky if you tend to lose things. That’s where digital IDs come in. Apple lets you add a virtual version of your driver’s license or state ID to your Wallet app, so you can securely verify your identity at airports, apps, and more. 

In this guide, I’ll explain why digital IDs are useful, what you need to get started, and how to add your driver’s license or state ID to Apple Wallet on your iPhone and Apple Watch.

Table of Contents
  • Why Use a Digital ID in Apple Wallet?
  • Device Requirements
  • Which States Have Apple Wallet Driver's License and ID
  • How to Add Your Driver's License or State ID to Apple Wallet
    • Verify Your Identity
    • Create Digital ID on Apple Watch
  • Transfer Your Driver’s License to a New iPhone
  • How to Use Your Digital ID in Apple Wallet
    • View ID Information
    • Present Driver's License In Person
    • Share Your ID with an App
  • Remove Your Driver's License or State ID From Apple Wallet
  • Troubleshoot Common Issues
  • Create Digital ID Using Passport in Apple Wallet
  • Digital IDs are the future!

Why Use a Digital ID in Apple Wallet? 

Adding your driver’s license or state ID to Apple Wallet makes your everyday life easier and safer. Here are the main reasons why:  

  • Convenience: With a digital ID, you don’t always have to carry your physical wallet. Whether you’re at the airport or using an app that needs age verification, your ID is just a tap away. 
  • Faster Access: At TSA checkpoints that support digital IDs, simply hold your iPhone or Apple Watch near the reader, no fumbling through your bag or wallet.  
  • More Secure Than a Physical Card: A plastic ID can be lost, stolen, or copied. In Apple Wallet, your digital ID is encrypted and stored securely in accordance with ISO 18013-5.
  • Privacy First: Only you can unlock it, using Face ID or your passcode. Also, Apple and your state’s DMV don’t track when or where you use your ID. 
  • Avoid the Risk of Identity Theft: When you show your physical ID, you expose all your information. However, with Apple Wallet, you can share only the specific details requested, like your date of birth or ID photo. 
  • Use Across Devices: You can access your driver’s license or state ID on your iPhone and Apple Watch without extra apps. 

Overall, a digital ID in Apple Wallet saves time, enhances privacy, and keeps you prepared for a world that’s going increasingly digital. 

Device Requirements 

To add a digital ID to Apple Wallet, you’ll need a few things.

  • Your device must be an iPhone 8 or later (or iPhone SE 2nd generation or newer) running iOS 15.4+.
  • Face ID or Touch ID must be set up and enabled on your iPhone.
  • For Apple Watch, it should be Series 4 or later with watchOS 8.4+.
  • You’ll also need an Apple ID with two-factor authentication enabled 
  • Your device’s region must be set to the United States.
  • A stable internet connection during setup.
  • A valid physical driver’s license or state ID card from a valid region.

Not all states support this feature yet, and availability varies by location. Apple partners with state governments to roll it out, so see if your state is included before beginning.  

Which States Have Apple Wallet Driver’s License and ID  

As of 2026, the following U.S. states and territories support a digital driver’s license or state ID in Apple Wallet: 

  • Arizona  
  • Maryland  
  • Colorado 
  • Georgia 
  • Ohio 
  • California 
  • Hawaii 
  • Iowa 
  • New Mexico 
  • Montana 
  • North Dakota
  • West Virginia
  • Illinois
  • Arkansas
  • Virginia

You can also use the feature in Puerto Rico.

Apple has also announced that several other regions, including North Carolina, Connecticut, Kentucky, Mississippi, Oklahoma, and Utah, may soon join the list.

Moreover, the U.K. government has also shown interest in launching a GOV.UK Wallet and App. So, the citizens can store a virtual version of their driver’s license.

Note Digital IDs are only valid in the issuing state for now, though they’re accepted at select TSA checkpoints nationwide.

How to Add Your Driver’s License or State ID to Apple Wallet 

Adding your ID to Apple Wallet is easy and takes just a few minutes. Note that you can link only one license or ID to your Apple Account. Here’s the process:

  1. Open the Wallet app on your iPhone and tap the + sign in the top-right corner.
  2. Scroll down and select Driver’s License and ID Cards.
  3. Choose your state from the list of supported ones.
  4. Decide whether you want to add the ID to your iPhone only or to a paired Apple Watch as well. You can add it to your Watch later if needed.
  5. Scan the front and back of your physical ID card with your iPhone’s camera, then tap Continue. Make sure it’s well-lit and flat on a dark surface for a clear scan.
  6. Follow the on-screen prompts to verify your identity (more on this in the next section).
  7. Once verified, your information is securely sent to your state’s issuing authority for approval. This can take a few minutes to a few hours.
  8. When approved, your digital ID will appear in Wallet. You’ll get a notification, and it will be ready to use.

Similarly, you can add your student ID to your Wallet app, ensuring quick access to your campus.

Important Your digital ID doesn’t replace your physical one; you still need to carry it by law in most places. But it’s a handy backup.

Verify Your Identity 

Verification is a key step to ensure the issuing authority smoothly approves your request for the digital ID. After scanning your physical license or ID card:

  1. Tap Get Started, and your iPhone will ask you to take a Live Photo, selfie, or scan your face using Face ID.
  2. Stand before a clean background like a white wall and ensure good lighting. Your face should be clearly visible.
  3. Apple suggests taking off any sunglasses, masks, hats, or other obstructive accessories.
  4. Now, hold your iPhone in front of you steadily
  5. You’ll need to perform simple head movements, like turning left and right or smiling, to create a 3D map of your face.
  6. Hold each movement until your phone vibrates, indicating success.
  7. Finally, authenticate your data using your Face ID or Touch ID.

This data is encrypted and sent to Apple and your state for matching against your ID photo.

If everything checks out, the process continues. If not, you might receive a notification to provide additional information. Tap the alert and follow the instructions on the authority’s website.

Create Digital ID on Apple Watch 

If you already have your driver’s license or state ID on your iPhone, you can add it to your Apple Watch.

  1. Open the Watch app on your iPhone, then tap the My Watch tab.
  2. Scroll down and select Wallet & Apple Pay.
  3. Here, you will see your license or ID displayed in the Other Cards on Your Phone section.
  4. Tap the Add button next to the card, then follow the prompts.

Transfer Your Driver’s License to a New iPhone

Switching to a new iPhone? Transferring your data, including your digital ID, is easy during setup:

  1. During the Setup Assistant on your new iPhone, when you reach the Quick Start or data transfer screen, select Transfer from your old iPhone.
  2. Once the basics are done, tap Wallet in the list of items to transfer.
  3. Select your driver’s license or state ID from the options.
  4. Follow the on-screen instructions, which may include verifying your identity again with Face ID.
  5. Finally, confirm your choice by tapping Continue.
  6. Your ID will reappear in the Wallet on the new device. If you skip this step, you can add it manually afterward, but you’ll need to go through the complete setup again.

If not using Quick Start, sign in using the same Apple ID on the new phone, go to Wallet, and add the ID again.

How to Use Your Digital ID in Apple Wallet 

After adding it, accessing your digital ID is easy and safe. It’s usable for verification at TSA security checkpoints, in mobile apps, or at merchants, bars, restaurants, and venues that accept it.

View ID Information 

To see your ID details:

  1. Open the Wallet app on your iPhone.
  2. Tap your driver’s license or state ID card.
  3. You will see recent usage history for privacy purposes.
  4. For more information, tap the (i) button and select Driver’s License Info or ID Info.
  5. Authenticate with Face ID or Touch ID.
  6. Scroll to view the details like your address, date of birth, height, eye color, etc.

Along with your personal information, Apple provides the contact details of your issuing authority. So, you may report any discrepancy.

Present Driver’s License In Person 

At participating airports’ TSA checkpoints, businesses, and venues:

  1. Go to the Wallet app. 
  2. Double-click the side button on your iPhone and authenticate your Face ID or Touch ID if required.
  3. Tap the card deck at the bottom and select your ID from the cards. 
  4. Hold your device near the identity reader.
  5. Now, you will see the requested information (like name and photo).
  6. To share it, double-click the side button again.
  7. The reader verifies it wirelessly via NFC, no need to hand over your phone. It may click your picture for verification.
  8. You will see a pop-up stating Done with a checkmark when successful.

If you want to use your Apple Watch, unlock your paired iPhone with biometrics. Then double-click the Watch side button at TSA and hold it up.

Note Digital ID is accepted at over 250 airports nationwide as of 2026. So, look for the checkpoint signs to confirm its availability. Otherwise, you need to use your physical card.

Share Your ID with an App 

When an app needs ID verification (like for age checks to order alcohol or applying for a credit card): 

  1. The app or app clip will prompt you to Verify with Apple Wallet or Continue with Apple Wallet. 
  2. Tap to open Wallet and select your ID. 
  3. Review the requested information, like your birthdate, picture, etc. It also shows why the app is requesting your details and how long it will store them. 
  4. If you’re comfortable, double-click the side button of your iPhone and authenticate your biometrics. 
  5. The app receives the info securely without seeing your full ID. 

Remove Your Driver’s License or State ID From Apple Wallet  

As I have mentioned earlier, you can only link one ID to your Apple Account. Therefore, if you’re about to move to another state or change your Apple ID, or in case your ID has expired, you must delete the current one before adding a new one. Here’s how: 

  1. Open the Wallet app and tap your license or ID. 
  2. Tap the info (i) button. 
  3. Scroll down and tap Remove Driver’s License or Remove This ID. 
  4. Confirm the action. Your state will be notified, and the ID will be deleted from your device and iCloud. 

Apple also recommends removing your digital IDs before giving away or selling your device. 

Troubleshoot Common Issues 

Sometimes things don’t go smoothly. Here are fixes for common problems: 

General errors: Update to the latest iOS, reset network settings, or sign out/in of your Apple ID. If stuck, contact Apple Support or your state’s DMV. 

Create Digital ID Using Passport in Apple Wallet 

With iOS 26.1, Apple introduced U.S. passport-based digital IDs. This means U.S. passport holders can add a secure digital version to Wallet, useful for domestic travel verification at TSA security checkpoints or additional identity proof.

The best part is that even if you don’t reside in a state that accepts digital IDs and driver’s licenses, you can still create an iPhone ID using your passport. It will work similarly to state IDs, with biometric protection and selective sharing. 

Moreover, iOS 26 introduced several new features in the Wallet app to ensure a smooth travel experience.  

  • Live boarding passes, airport maps, and luggage tracking via AirTags enhance the travel experience in the Wallet app.  
  • Verify with Wallet expands beyond apps to websites (e.g., for age checks or identity verification). 

Digital IDs are the future!

Apple Wallet’s digital IDs provide a convenient, secure, and modern way to present your driver’s license or state ID. With just a few simple steps, you can ditch the physical card in many situations. As more states come on board and new features in iOS 26 approach, now is the perfect time to get started if your state supports it.

What do you think about this tech-savvy feature? Let me know in the comments below!

keyPoints.title: Benefits of Digital IDs in Apple Wallet
keyPoints.explanation: Digital IDs offer convenience, faster TSA checks, enhanced security, privacy, and device compatibility, making daily identity verification safer and easier.

keyPoints.title: Requirements & Availability for Digital IDs
keyPoints.explanation: To add a digital ID, you need an iPhone 8 or later with iOS 15.4+, Face or Touch ID enabled, and support from your state, as well as an Apple ID with two-factor authentication.

keyPoints.title: Supported States and Regions
keyPoints.explanation: As of 2025, states like Arizona, Maryland, Colorado, and others support digital IDs, with plans for more regions, including the UK, to adopt the technology soon.

keyPoints.title: How to Add Your Digital ID to Apple Wallet
keyPoints.explanation: Adding your ID involves opening the Wallet app, selecting your state, scanning your physical ID, and verifying your identity through a secure process on your iPhone.

keyPoints.title: Using and Managing Your Digital ID
keyPoints.explanation: Your digital ID can be viewed, used at TSA, shared with apps, transferred to new devices, or removed from Wallet when no longer needed or upon moving.

title.rendered: M6 Mac mini is $300 more than the M4: Is it worth the upgrade?

content.rendered:
Apple has launched its new Mac mini powered by the M6 chip, bringing faster performance, improved graphics, better AI capabilities, and upgraded connectivity. But with the new model costing $300 more than the M4 Mac mini did at launch, my first thought was: Is the M6 Mac mini really worth the extra money, or is the M4 still the best to buy?

If you are also contemplating the same, here’s the answer. I will break down the M6 Mac mini vs. the M4 Mac mini, comparing their specs, benchmarks, performance, and price. So you can decide which Mac mini to buy in 2026.

M6 Mac mini vs M4 Mac mini: What’s actually different?

The M4 Mac mini already delivers remarkable performance for a tiny desktop. The M6 pushes considerably further, but it also changes the value equation.

M6 Mac mini vs M4 Mac mini performance: How big is the jump?

The M6 uses Apple’s first 2nm chip design and adds two CPU cores and two GPU cores compared with the M4. It also introduces a dual 16-core Neural Engine and increases maximum memory from 24GB to 32GB. That is a serious generational upgrade on paper.

CPU: M6 adds two more cores

The M4 Mac mini uses a 10-core CPU with four performance cores and six efficiency cores. The M6 moves to a 12-core CPU comprising two super cores, four performance cores, and six efficiency cores. This new higher-performance core design is aimed at improving single-threaded workloads.

Apple claims the M6 delivers up to 40% faster CPU performance than the M4, while multi-core performance can be up to 1.2x faster. It also increases memory bandwidth from 120GB/s on M4 to 170GB/s on M6, giving the CPU, GPU, and AI hardware more data to work with.

Early reports estimate that the Geekbench 7 single-core score could rise from roughly 3,277 on the M4 to around 4,590 on the M6, while the multi-core score could rise from about 15,359 to 18,431.

GPU: This is where the M6 gets seriously interesting

The M4 has a 10-core GPU, while the M6 steps up to a 12-core GPU. But the bigger change isn’t simply the extra cores. Every M6 GPU core includes a Neural Accelerator, giving the chip considerably more AI-focused graphics hardware. Apple claims the M6 can deliver up to 2x faster graphics performance than the M4 and up to 4x the peak AI compute.

For gamers, creative professionals, and anyone using AI-heavy applications, this could be a much more noticeable upgrade.

AI performance: The M6 pulls further ahead

The M4 has a 16-core Neural Engine. The M6 uses a dual 16-core Neural Engine, alongside Neural Accelerators built into its GPU cores. Apple claims the new Neural Engine delivers twice the performance of the previous generation and says LLM prompt processing in LM Studio can be up to 4.8x faster than on M4.

Bottom line: the M6 is a meaningful performance upgrade. But whether you’ll notice the difference depends entirely on what you do with your Mac mini. For demanding workloads, running local AI, and building agentic workflows, the M6 is definitely better than the M4. Otherwise, the M4 will serve most users well.

The memory upgrade matters

Here’s an upgrade that deserves more attention than it is getting. The M6 Mac mini supports up to 32GB of unified memory, compared with 24GB on the M4. Memory bandwidth also rises from 120GB/s to as much as 170GB/s.

For a basic user, that’s irrelevant. But if you’re running multiple professional applications, large datasets, virtual machines, local AI models, or increasingly memory-hungry workflows, it could be the difference between “this works” and “this is comfortable.”

And because unified memory is shared between the CPU and GPU, having more of it can be particularly useful for workloads that mix traditional computing with graphics or AI. If you are buying an M6, spend money on memory before obsessing over tiny storage benchmarks. You can’t add RAM later.

M6 Mac mini comes with better networking and connectivity

When it comes to physical ports, the M6 Mac mini vs M4 Mac mini comparison is surprisingly close. Apple has kept almost the exact same port layout, so this isn’t a generation where you’ll suddenly get a bunch of new connectors.

The bigger changes are networking and wireless connectivity.

The M6 also adds support for two external displays with variable refresh rate over a single Thunderbolt port. The real upgrade is networking. If you regularly move large files across a fast local network, use network-attached storage, or have a high-speed home network, you will see better speeds.

So, should ports and connectivity be a reason to upgrade?

Probably not if you already own an M4. The physical port selection hasn’t changed enough to justify replacing the machine by itself. But if you’re buying a Mac mini for a new setup, and especially if you have a fast home network, the M6’s 2.5Gb Ethernet, Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6 make it the more future-ready choice.

The M6 Mac mini price increase is real

Now we get to the uncomfortable part.

Apple has set the M6 Mac mini‘s starting price at $899, with 16GB of unified memory and 256GB of storage. That’s $100 more than the M4 Mac mini’s latest $799 price, but the bigger shock is that the M4 originally launched at just $599 in 2024

Memory upgrades are exactly the same as before: moving from 16GB to 24GB costs $200, while going from 24GB to 32GB costs another $200.

Storage follows a similar pattern, but the pricing changes as you move up the ladder. Going from 256GB to 512GB costs $200. Moving to 1TB costs another $300, while stepping all the way up to 2TB adds another $500. That means Apple’s internal SSD remains the expensive part of the configuration.

M4 Mac mini: Why it still makes sense

The M4 Mac mini is still very powerful. For everyday productivity, web browsing, office work, coding, photo management, streaming, light-to-moderate creative work, and general home computing, there’s very little reason to feel deprived by choosing M4.

In fact, if you can find an M4 at a significant discount, the value proposition gets even stronger.

The M4 already brought a major redesign and a substantial performance leap over previous generations. It supports Apple Intelligence, hardware-accelerated ray tracing, and multi-display workflows, while its compact design makes it unusually easy to integrate into an existing desk setup.

So if someone asks me, “Should I buy M6 or M4?” my response is: Buy the M4 if saving money is the priority. Buy the M6 if buying new and keeping it for years is the priority.

Who should buy the M6 Mac mini?

The M6 makes the most sense for these users:

  • People buying their first Mac mini: If you’re starting from scratch, the decision is easier. Why buy the previous generation when the new generation costs $100 more and offers substantially higher performance, newer connectivity, and a longer runway?
  • Local AI enthusiasts: This is perhaps the strongest reason to choose M6. The improved Neural Engine, GPU Neural Accelerators, higher memory ceiling, and increased memory bandwidth are designed for AI-intensive workloads.
  • Creative professionals: Video editing, graphics, photo processing, 3D work, and other sustained workloads can take advantage of the M6’s stronger GPU and faster storage.
  • People keeping the machine for five years: This is the sleeper argument for M6. A $100 premium spread over five years is only $20 per year.

Who should stick with the M4?

Almost everyone else.

If you’re primarily browsing, writing, streaming, managing email, using Microsoft Office, doing schoolwork, coding without extreme workloads, or editing the occasional photo or video, the M4 is already overqualified.

That’s why I wouldn’t recommend upgrading from M4 simply because the M6 exists.

What about the M5 Pro Mac mini?

This is where Apple’s lineup gets more interesting.

The M5 Pro Mac mini starts at $1,699, compared with $899 for the M6 model. Apple positions it squarely at professionals handling demanding workloads such as video production, game development, scientific simulations, 3D work, and large AI models.

The M5 Pro can scale to an 18-core CPU, 20-core GPU, 64GB of unified memory, and 307GB/s memory bandwidth. It also gets Thunderbolt 5, while the M6 model uses Thunderbolt 4.

So, should you buy an M6 or M5 Pro Mac mini?

  • For normal users: M6.
  • For professional users whose workloads routinely consume CPU cores, GPU resources, memory, or bandwidth: M5 Pro.

If you’re rendering 3D scenes, working with huge datasets, editing demanding video projects, developing games, or running serious local AI models, the extra $800 can make sense.

Final verdict: Is the M6 Mac mini worth the upgrade?

The M6 Mac mini upgrade is worth it if you’re coming from an older Mac, building a new setup, running demanding workloads, or planning to keep the machine for years. Apple has made a genuinely substantial generational upgrade.

But the M4 remains fast enough that most owners won’t suddenly discover a new category of things they can do.

For a new buyer? I would wait for M6 discounts if you’re price-sensitive. And I would absolutely consider an M4 if retailers start clearing inventory aggressively.

title.rendered: GTA 6 Cyberleek leaks timeline: Everything we know so far

content.rendered:
GTA 6 leaks have been the talk of the town for nearly a week, as the hacker group known as Cyberleek has been relentlessly dropping at least one new video every day. These leaked clips have revealed a lot of previously unverified information, particularly about GTA 6’s gameplay. This is one aspect that Rockstar Games has still not talked about much, which should change with August 27’s official extended look.

Even before Rockstar Games released the first trailer for GTA 6, the game had already been hit with a major leak giving a very early look at what the devs were cooking. The latest leak, coordinated by hackers who champion gamers’ rights in their “manifesto” but don’t shy away from marketing their memecoin in their videos, is similar, if not bigger, in terms of magnitude.

As spotted by sources including PC Gamer, the Tate McRae song “Sports Car”, released in January 2025, was found to be playing on the radio in one of these GTA 6 leaks. Keeping this in mind, it’s logical to assume the leaked videos show a build of the game at least from some time last year.

Below, you can find the compilation of all the GTA 6 information unveiled in the leaks posted by Cyberleek. The list is put together in chronological order and will be updated in the future as and when new leaks from the same group surface online.

All GTA 6 details leaked by Cyberleek

Leak 1: Basketball minigame (August 18)

This is where it all started; the first leak that showed some GTA 6 gameplay as Jason. It showed the co-protagonist playing basketball at his safehouse. The pastime is apparently available as a minigame, and you can see the counter for the number of baskets you score. A small glimpse of the game’s water physics was also shown, courtesy of a stray rebound putting the ball in the water.

Glimpses of the stamina bar and what looks like a focus bar—akin to what we saw in 2018’s Red Dead Redemption 2—appear in the HUD. Notably, the HUD also confirmed that money in possession was separated from money at a safehouse/in the bank, as two different account balances were displayed on the screen.

It was also around this time that the entire GTA 6 map was leaked, showing Vice City and the various other regions in the state of Leonida. The other prominent locations in the game, besides the neon-lit beach city, are the larger Vice-Dale County, Mariana County, Kelly County, Lummox County, and Leonard County.

Leak 2: First look at driving, combat, and wanted system (August 18)

This video showed Jason driving a Vapid ’70 Ganado recklessly, leading to a road rage altercation with an NPC. Owing to the fistfight that followed, we got to see hand-to-hand combat in GTA 6 for the first time, alongside the use of a melee weapon (wrench). After Jason apparently killed that NPC, an evil emoji with a minus sign appeared, which hinted at an RDR 2-like honor system.

Upon committing the crime, GTA 6’s male lead gained a two-star wanted level, which also confirmed the return of the six-star wanted level system last seen in GTA 4. In the latest rendition, the cops apparently remember the appearance, outfit, and vehicle of the player character during a police chase.

Jason can also see color-changing indicators pointing to where enemies are coming from and their alert status. This gameplay mechanic is similar to what is there in existing open-world games such as Ubisoft’s Watch Dogs series. Moreover, during the ‘wanted’ sequence, it was notable that the minimap no longer showed the exact position of cops right away—a change from GTA 5.

Important this was also the leak that gave us a first glimpse at the fuel meter for the vehicle and the ability to store weapons and items in the trunk. Also, the option to reply to NPCs positively or negatively, as in RDR 2, was also featured.

Leak 3: More combat and taser gun (August 19)

The third leak showed Jason carry out an onslaught on a restricted facility’s security guards. A bit of the game’s destruction physics were on show, as the video showed the boom barrier break exactly at the point of impact with Jason’s vehicle. When the player was near someone else’s vehicle, the options “Clone Key” and “Smash Window” popped up, showing two different ways cars can be stolen in the game.

In the intense combat that followed, the GTA 6 co-protagonist is shown making quick work of security personnel, giving a look at the swift fighting animations, disarming, and slow-mo knockout camera perspective. The fight involved Jason using his handgun (Klose K17) as a melee weapon and then a Shocker to tase enemies.

There was also a player-selectable option to “Surrender” shown during this confrontation. Meanwhile, the ability to equip accessories dropped by NPCs, such as a security personnel cap, was also shown. The video’s gameplay part ended with the player character hijacking an MTL Packer truck and escaping the facility amid gunfire.

At the end of the leak, there was a small cutscene featuring Jason and Cal Hampton on a boat. This part more or less confirmed that it wasn’t just gameplay but also story bits that Cyberleek may have access to.

Leak 4: Motorcycle traversal and performance-enhancing drug use (August 19)

This particular leak offered a good look at GTA 6’s weapon wheel, which has two separate tabs for “Weapons” and “Items”. While there are 8 weapon slots, including the unarmed/fist option, the Items tab wasn’t switched to and hence not revealed. The Weapons tab also showed two slots for what appear to be drugs, one of which is Zombix, which Jason uses in the video. A game prompt also noted that repeated usage of the drug led to temporarily receiving a weaker buff from it.

Leak 4 further shed light on the ability to pick up or loot downed enemies. This approach means NPCs no longer automatically drop cash upon dying and makes GTA 6 more realistic, just as RDR 2 did, which employed the same mechanics.

It also shared the first look at motorcycle handling and swimming physics. A button prompt to “Dive” also appeared when Jason was in water, all but confirming an underwater world will once again be there for exploration in GTA 6, like how it was in GTA 5.

Leak 5: Aircraft traversal and gunplay (August 20)

Through this video leak, anticipating fans got their first look at flying aircraft in GTA 6. In it, Jason is shown piloting a crop duster through the skies of Leonida. The impressive draw distance means that the horizon goes far back and much of the state is visible from the sky at any point.

As was the case in RDR 2, there are volumetric clouds in GTA 6 as well. The shadows, lighting, and details from the sky looked quite good in the clip, but there were a few pop-ins nonetheless.

Besides the praiseworthy graphical fidelity, the fifth leaked footage also showed the radio selection screen. It had two options: “Radio,” which showed all of Vice City’s radio stations and an “On Demand” option, which wasn’t selected by the leaker in this clip but probably is an in-game equivalent of Spotify and similar online music streaming services.

One of the most interesting parts of this video was, near the end, when Jason sprayed bullets onto a wall, writing “LEAK” on it. This made it very likely that the hackers behind it were not dealing with illegally obtained clips but possibly an entire unofficial build.

Leak 6: Sports car traversal (August 21)

Relatively simple and uneventful, this leak showed Jason hijacking a sports car, which confirmed that throwing out a driver from his seat won’t be as easy as a single button-press, like in past GTA games, and might require some brief button-mashing.

The rest of the video shows the player cruising through the city roads and navigating through traffic, giving a good peek at the game’s eye-catchingly detailed world. The textures and reflections look very good, with no noticeable pop-in.

Leak 7: Store robbery gameplay (August 22)

Leak 7 let us know that the gas stations in GTA 6 also offer a repair service for the player’s car, besides refueling. The video showed Jason assaulting a gas station convenience store employee and stealing money from the cash counter. After gaining a two-star wanted level and evading the cops, he is shown robbing another nearby gas station.

While escaping the police, Jason’s car collides with another vehicle, which triggers a slow-motion cinematic camera, suggesting that major car crashes might be shown in that manner. The leak closed out with the player entering a strip club, teasing the focus of the next leaked video.

Leak 8: Strip club (August 22)

This leak continued from where the preceding one left off and showed the player exploring a strip club known as Delights Cabaret. There is a good amount of NPC density in this closed space and, obviously, a lot of partial nudity is on display.

Leak 9: Gas station NPC encounter, first look at ‘Wasted’ (August 22)

The HD-era GTA games revolutionized how NPCs go about their own life while the player takes on the story by giving some of them their own quirky actions and dialogues. One such unique NPC behavior was on full display in the ninth leaked video. In it, a conspiracy theorist can be seen filling gas in the bathtub stored in his pickup truck’s trunk. Strangely, the NPC animation during this scene was visibly all over the place.

As the video continues, Jason steals the fuel-filled truck and runs over the chasing NPC, the vehicle’s owner. Just as he takes the stolen vehicle onto the road, another vehicle crashes into the GTA 6 main character, instantly causing an explosion and concluding with the “Wasted” screen.

Right at the end of the clip, it skips to another scene where Jason is in the restroom and the prompt “Return to Lucia” appears, suggesting it was footage possibly from a dating side-activity.

Leak 10: Aircraft traversal, Vice City at night (August 23)

In another instance of Jason piloting a fixed-wing aircraft, this video flaunted the Vice City skyline during nighttime. While the visuals looked beautiful from above, there were significantly more pop-in issues with lighting and objects throughout the segment. A brief prompt telling the player about a fishing location for “Common Snook” basically confirmed the addition of fishing as a side activity in GTA 6.

Leak 11: Nudist town (August 24)

This one is the most explicit GTA 6 leak that has come out so far. It showed Jason entering what looks like a nudist gathering. There was full male and female nudity on display throughout the entirety of this leaked clip.

Near the end, Jason is confronted and attacked by another NPC for ogling her through his binoculars. Interestingly, despite the player eventually killing that NPC and some more, there is no wanted level gained—unlike the previous instances where he got one instantly. This hints at different rates of police reporting for cities and for isolated places.

Leak 12: Nightclub (August 25)

This leak saw Jason entering the Nine1Nine nightclub and exploring the place. The interior of the club showed the most crowd density in a closed space compared to all the Cyberleek clips thus far.

A highlight of this sequence is when the player character automatically starts rhythmically nodding his head when he is on the dance floor. There was also a button prompt to “Dance”, which Jason did for some moments, but the dance moves were very basic and hence forgettable.

During the final stretch of this leak, Jason can be seen interacting with NPCs. With the last character that he interacts with, we also see another button prompt for a service that costs $50. Although the watermark in the leak obscured the text of that prompt, it seemingly contained the word “Dance” at the end.

Leak 13: Beach (August 25)

Leak 13 showed Jason riding a bicycle through a crowded beach, with impressive population density and variety. This scene also included birds interacting on the terrain. Despite the beach being a highly active venue with lots of NPCs, there were no visible performance struggles observed in the video. The lighting, shadows, and water physics in the leak looked good as well.

Leak 14: Game Store (August 25)

With this video, Cyberleek shared an unprecedented count of three different video leaks within a span of 24 hours. This clip showed Jason visiting a game shop called Game Horde in Port Gellhorn. A brief glimpse early in the video showed an option, “Break In,” next to a car’s trunk, implying that we may be able to loot these storage spaces separately in GTA 6.

The store’s interior was chock-full of physical games, gaming consoles, laptops, tech accessories, arcade machines, and more. Based on the button prompts alone, it can be deduced that Jason can play on functional arcade machines and also purchase different phone cases. And, from the purchase options explored in the leak, it was confirmed that different kinds of earbuds and headphones would be available to buy, too.

Leak 15: Modded car, Lucia first appearance (August 26)

In the opening moments of this leak, Jason ousts an NPC from his modified Declasse ’80 Impaler and takes it for a ride. The car, notably, has a Rideout Customs sticker on the rear window, green-tinted windows, and neon pink lighting underneath the car chassis.

In the following police chase, the player can be seen heading towards a heart marker on the mini-map, which could possibly be for a mission or a side-activity with Lucia. The location in the clip was eventually determined to be the Jack Of Hearts strip club. Near the end, there is a very brief tease of a cutscene featuring both GTA 6 protagonists, making it the first time Lucia is shown in these string of leaks.

Leak 16: Lucia prologue (August 26)

Spoiler Alert: The following text contains story spoiler for GTA 6

Leak 16 did what was long expected in the community to not be on the cards, it gave us a cutscene and gameplay segment centered on Lucia for the very first time. In it, Cyberleek claimed that it had access to a build that was “actually recent” and that the game was “not ready at all,” even going as far as saying Rockstar was “killing their own employees” by allegedly pushing them to do “way too much” work with “so little time left” until launch.

The leaked video begins with an incarcerated Lucia looking out the door window, as a flashback from nine months ago follows right after and shows the financial struggles of the first female GTA protagonist in years. The background music at the very beginning of this cutscene and the big “Prologue” text at its end suggest this part might be among the earliest moments in the game’s story.

After that, the game resumes into a gameplay sequence where Lucia can interact with her cellmates, who appear to be four in total excluding GTA 6’s co-protagonist. The player interacts with one of them, Yolanda, before being summoned by a police guard named “Wilson.” Interestingly, Wilson seems to have a cordial attitude towards Lucia and their conversation even hints at the guard colluding with her for bringing in something illegal into the penitentiary.

There is nothing else major shown in the leak, besides Lucia exploring the facility’s corridors and “social room.” The brief chat between her and Wilson revealed that she was headed to her routine counselor meeting which was to be presided over by a woman called “Gates.” It was also shared that her original counselor, Mr Reigns, was relieved for supposed misconduct with another female inmate.

GTA 6 leaks: What to expect next

Ever since the spree of leaks started, Cyberleek has been conducting a poll for what it should show next. With GTA 6 Extended Look soon to have its Netflix premiere, you would think the hacker group would pump out as many leaks now as they can. In that case, you can expect information obtained from those leaks to be added to this article promptly, and with story spoiler warnings if needed.

Rather anticlimactically, a chunk of GTA 6’s gameplay and features have already been shared online before Rockstar’s own official outlets could do that. However, there should be lots of more to see during the 30-minute Extended Look airing that takes place on Thursday at 12 PM PT or 3 PM ET on the aforementioned OTT platform, followed by a YouTube premiere six hours later.

It will be interesting to see how the content and pattern of Cyberleek’s GTA 6 videos change after the official showcase. In the meantime, Rockstar Games has one eye on its efforts to track down the hacker group as soon as possible, which is another intriguing story to track in parallel.

mainEntity.name: 1. How many Sonic The Hedgehog character skins are available in Fortnite?

acceptedAnswer.text: At the time of writing, there are four different Sonic franchise characters up for grabs, namely Sonic, Dr Eggman, Knuckles, and Shadow.

mainEntity.name: 2. Can I get the Sonic the Hedgehog skin from the Item Shop?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, you must purchase the Fortnite Override Battle Pass to get the Sonic skin as it isn't available in the Shop.

mainEntity.name: 3. Is Tails available in Fortnite?

acceptedAnswer.text: While Tails is not available in Fortnite as a skin, you can still unlock his sidekick version by purchasing the Battle Pass for Chapter 7 Season 4 and reaching Level 2.
