title.rendered: I tried using ChatGPT inside the new Siri AI app, and there’s one annoying catch

content.rendered:
Apple has finally made Siri feel less like a voice assistant and more like a proper AI chatbot. In iOS 27, iPadOS 27, and macOS 27, the new Siri AI app offers a conversational interface that will feel surprisingly familiar if you already use ChatGPT, Claude, or Grok.

The exciting thing is that although Siri is powered by Google’s Gemini model behind the scenes, you can switch to ChatGPT as an alternative AI provider. I spent some time asking ChatGPT, instead of Siri, on my iPhone in the new app. Here’s how the feature works, what it’s like to use, and whether it’s actually worth replacing the ChatGPT app.

What’s changed with Siri in OS 27?

The biggest change isn’t simply that Siri got smarter. Apple has turned Siri into an app.

With iOS 27, iPadOS 27, and macOS 27, you get a dedicated Siri AI experience that looks and behaves much more like a conventional AI chatbot. You can start conversations, type questions, use your voice, and return to previous Siri conversations later. Apple also syncs Siri conversations across devices through iCloud.

That makes the old Siri-versus-ChatGPT relationship considerably more interesting.

Previously, ChatGPT was essentially Siri’s backup plan. Whenever I asked a complicated question that Siri couldn’t answer, it would ask for my permission to send the request to ChatGPT. You could also explicitly prompt Siri to use ChatGPT to answer questions, create images, explain what’s on your screen, and more.

The new Siri app flips that experience around. Instead of waiting for Siri to decide that a question is too complicated, you can choose ChatGPT yourself. That’s the part I like most. If I want ChatGPT to handle something where I prefer its style or capabilities over Gemini-powered Siri, I can explicitly select ChatGPT.

How to use ChatGPT inside the Siri app on iPhone or iPad

Getting ChatGPT working inside the new Siri app is surprisingly straightforward.

Before starting, make sure you have a compatible iPhone or iPad running iOS 27 or iPadOS 27 and that you’ve already set up the new Siri AI experience by going to Settings > Siri > and tapping Try New Siri.

Note: iOS 27 and iPadOS 27 are currently in beta, so the interface may change before the final release.

Once you’re ready:

  1. Open the Siri app.
  2. Start a new conversation by tapping the compose button.
  3. Now, tap and hold the Ask Siri typing field.
  4. Select Ask from the pop-up menu, then choose ChatGPT from the options.
  5. Look at the input field. The placeholder changes from Ask Siri to Ask ChatGPT.

That’s how you know OpenAI is now handling your questions instead of Siri. From there, simply type your prompt or ask your question.

How to use ChatGPT inside Siri on Mac

The process is almost identical on Mac, although the interaction is slightly different.

On a Mac running macOS 27 Golden Gate:

  1. Open the Siri app.
  2. Start a new conversation.
  3. Control-click inside the Ask Siri field.
  4. Select Ask and choose ChatGPT from the drop-down.
  5. Start typing your question.

The input field changes to Ask ChatGPT, confirming that ChatGPT is now handling the conversation.

I like the consistency here. Apple hasn’t created a completely different workflow for Mac users. The basic idea remains the same: open Siri, choose the AI assistant you want, and start chatting.

What happens when you switch between Siri and ChatGPT?

This is where using the feature becomes more interesting. Siri and ChatGPT don’t behave like two completely separate apps. They can take turns handling the same conversational space.

During my testing, I found that after switching to ChatGPT, asking “Who are you?” results in an answer stating that ChatGPT is assisting me. Then, saying “Is it the Siri app?” surprisingly shifts the conversation from ChatGPT back to Siri. That’s a neat trick because it makes the experience feel fluid. You aren’t necessarily locked into one AI for the entire conversation.

But the reverse behavior is much less elegant. If you ask Siri to “Switch to ChatGPT,” it doesn’t simply change the provider inside the Siri conversation. Instead, it opened the standalone ChatGPT app on my iPhone as it was already installed.

That’s exactly the kind of inconsistency that makes me think this feature still needs some polishing. Apple has created a menu for choosing ChatGPT, so I would rather see that choice work consistently in both directions.

The annoying catch: ChatGPT doesn’t stay selected

This is the biggest problem I found. ChatGPT is not a permanent setting in the new Siri app. You can select it to use it. But then Siri quietly forgets your preference.

In my testing, the app switches back to Siri when you:

  • Start a new conversation.
  • Leave a conversation and return to it.
  • Close and reopen the Siri app.

There is currently no setting that lets you permanently set ChatGPT as the default AI provider in the Siri app.

And honestly, this is the part I would want Apple to change first. If I deliberately choose ChatGPT, there’s a good chance I chose it because I want ChatGPT to handle my next questions too. Making me select it again every time isn’t a major inconvenience, but it is unnecessary friction.

Another catch: Siri ChatGPT conversations don’t appear in ChatGPT history

This limitation surprised me even more. You might reasonably assume that signing into your OpenAI account would make conversations started with ChatGPT inside Siri appear in your normal ChatGPT history.

They don’t. Any questions I ask through ChatGPT in the Siri app don’t appear in my ChatGPT account history, even after signing in to my OpenAI account through the device’s Siri and ChatGPT settings.

That’s important because it creates two separate ChatGPT experiences.

There’s:

  • ChatGPT inside the Siri app
  • ChatGPT inside the ChatGPT app

They may both be powered by OpenAI, but your conversation history isn’t treated the same way.

For me, this makes the Siri integration much less compelling for anything I expect to revisit later. If I’m researching something, brainstorming an article, working on a project, or asking a question whose answer I’ll need tomorrow, I’d rather use the ChatGPT app.

What to do if ChatGPT isn’t showing up

If you don’t see ChatGPT as an option inside the Siri app, don’t assume the feature is broken.

The first thing to check is that the ChatGPT extension is enabled for Siri.

On iPhone, iPad, or Mac:

  1. Open Settings on iPhone/iPad or System Settings on Mac.
  2. Go to Siri and select ChatGPT.
  3. Make sure Use Extension is enabled.
  4. Return to the Siri app.
  5. Try selecting ChatGPT again.

If it still doesn’t work, quit the Siri app and reopen it. As a final resort, restart the device and try again.

It’s worth remembering that we’re dealing with beta software here. Apple is still refining iOS 27, iPadOS 27, and macOS 27, so odd behavior shouldn’t necessarily be treated as a permanent limitation.

Does this replace the ChatGPT app?

No. Not for me.

And I don’t think that’s necessarily a bad thing. ChatGPT inside Siri is useful precisely because it gives you another AI option without forcing you to leave Apple’s Siri environment.

But the dedicated ChatGPT app is still the better choice if ChatGPT is your primary AI assistant.

Here’s how I see it.

Use ChatGPT inside Siri when:

  • You already live in Apple’s Siri ecosystem.
  • You want a quick answer from ChatGPT.
  • You don’t want to switch apps for a single question.
  • You want to choose between Siri and ChatGPT depending on the task.
  • You don’t care about keeping the conversation in ChatGPT history.

Use the ChatGPT app when:

  • ChatGPT is your main AI assistant.
  • You want a reliable conversation history.
  • You’re working on a longer project.
  • You expect to return to the conversation later.
  • You want the full ChatGPT experience rather than an AI provider embedded inside Siri.

For quick questions, Siri’s implementation is genuinely convenient.

For serious ChatGPT use, I’ll still open ChatGPT.

Could Claude, Grok, or other AI assistants be added?

ChatGPT isn’t necessarily the only third-party AI service that could eventually appear inside Siri.

Industry leaks have suggested Apple is open to giving other AI services a similar level of integration, with names such as Claude and Grok being obvious possibilities. The exact plans aren’t confirmed, so this should be treated as a possibility rather than a promised feature.

If Apple actually opens Siri to multiple AI providers, I think the current ChatGPT integration starts to make much more sense.

Imagine opening Siri and choosing:

  • Siri/Gemini for Apple’s assistant features.
  • ChatGPT for certain kinds of questions.
  • Claude for coding or another type of task.
  • Grok for another.

That would turn Siri into something more interesting than another chatbot. It could become the front door to multiple AI assistants.

Enjoy advanced Siri with ChatGPT!

I like ChatGPT inside the new Siri app. I just don’t love the way Apple has implemented it.

For the first time, I can open Siri, decide that I want ChatGPT, and have OpenAI handle the question without treating ChatGPT as some emergency backup Siri calls when it gets stuck. That’s a meaningful improvement over the old Siri-to-ChatGPT experience.

But every new conversation effectively sends me back to Siri, so I have to choose ChatGPT again, and the conversations don’t appear in my normal ChatGPT history. That makes the Siri version feel temporary. It’s great for asking something and moving on, but less appealing when I’m doing work I want to keep.

Will you use ChatGPT inside the Siri app? Let me know your thoughts in the comments below!

mainEntity.name: 1. How many Sonic The Hedgehog character skins are available in Fortnite?

acceptedAnswer.text: At the time of writing, there are four different Sonic franchise characters up for grabs, namely Sonic, Dr Eggman, Knuckles, and Shadow.

mainEntity.name: 2. Can I get the Sonic the Hedgehog skin from the Item Shop?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, you must purchase the Fortnite Override Battle Pass to get the Sonic skin as it isn't available in the Shop.

mainEntity.name: 3. Is Tails available in Fortnite?

acceptedAnswer.text: While Tails is not available in Fortnite as a skin, you can still unlock his sidekick version by purchasing the Battle Pass for Chapter 7 Season 4 and reaching Level 2.

title.rendered: DOORS codes (August 2026)

content.rendered:
Update: Verified the latest Doors Codes on August 26, 2026

DOORS can end a good Hotel run with one bad hiding spot, so every free Knob helps. Knobs buy useful pre-run items, while Stardust is handy for cosmetic rewards. The working codes below give you 210 Knobs and 4 Stardust without spending Robux. Redeem them before your next run, especially the ones with spaces or symbols that are annoying to type by hand.

All working DOORS codes

  • FE4R_RBX: 5 Knobs (NEW)
  • NO_DATA: 5 Knobs (NEW)
  • /E FREE: 1 Knob (NEW)
  • LAZYDEVS: 50 Knobs
  • 3rd: Get 33 Knobs
  • RAGDOLL COMBAT: Get 1 Stardust
  • PATHSWAP: Get 1 Stardust
  • JUMP OVER THE BRICK: Get 1 Stardust
  • VOCAB HAVOC: Get 1 Stardust
  • SCREECHSUCKS: 25 Knobs
  • 8BITRYAN: 5 Knobs
  • ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ: 5 Knobs
  • BIJUU MIKE: 5 Knobs
  • DANTDM: 5 Knobs
  • FIND THE TROLLFACES: 5 Knobs
  • ISHOWSPEED: 5 Knobs
  • KREEKCRAFT: 5 Knobs
  • KUBZ SCOUTS: 5 Knobs
  • LORE: 5 Knobs
  • PENGUINZ0: 5 Knobs
  • RAGDOLL MAYHEM: 5 Knobs
  • RAGDOLL UNIVERSE: 5 Knobs
  • THINKNOODLES: 5 Knobs
  • W: 5 Knobs
  • XQC: 5 Knobs
  • 41: 5 Knobs
  • 54: 5 Knobs
  • 67: 5 Knobs
  • CHEDDAR BALLS: 1 Knob
  • CRUSADERS: 5 Stardust
  • Gullible: Nothing
  • L: Nothing
  • E FREE: 1 Knob

Expired DOORS codes

1000, 100MVISITS, 2BILLIONVISITS, 4B, 500MVISITS, 5B, 777, GRACE, LOOKBEHINDYOU, ONEBILLIONVISITS, ONEBLLIONVISITS, PRESSURE, PSST, SIX2025, SORRYBOUTTHAT, SORRYFORDELAY, TEST, THEHUNT, THREE

How to redeem DOORS codes

The code box sits inside the lobby Store, so you can claim everything before starting a run.

  1. Open DOORS on Roblox.
  2. Select Store at the bottom of the lobby screen.
  3. Paste a working code into the box at the top.
  4. Press the check mark to claim the reward.

Why your DOORS code is not working

Most failed redemptions have a simple cause:

  • The code expired: LSPLASH can remove milestone or event codes without warning.
  • You already used it: Each reward code works once per Roblox account.
  • A space or symbol is missing: Capitalization does not matter, but /E FREE, FE4R_RBX, and the multi-word codes need their spaces and symbols.
  • Your server is old: Leave the experience and join a fresh server when a newly reactivated code fails.
  • The code gives nothing: CRUSADERS and L redeem successfully but do not add a usable reward.

If a reward code still fails after a clean copy-paste in a fresh server, treat it as expired and move on.

Where to find more DOORS codes

New codes usually appear around major updates, anniversaries, milestones, or apology drops. Watch the DOORS account on X, join the LSPLASH Discord, and check the LSPLASH Roblox community when a big patch lands.

The social feeds move quickly, so bookmark this page if you want the useful codes without digging through every announcement. You can also find DOORS in our picks for the Haze Piece codes, Evade codes or browse the complete list of all Roblox game codes for more free rewards.

title.rendered: I’d pick these Pixel 11 Pro Fold cases over Google’s official case

content.rendered:
Buying a $1,899 foldable and then putting it in the first case Google recommends feels like the easy move. I’m not convinced it’s the smart one.

The Pixel 11 Pro Fold is far more complicated to protect than a regular slab phone. You need to think about the hinge, the cover and inner folding display, wireless charging, grip, and how much bulk you’re willing to add. The best Fold case, therefore, isn’t necessarily the one with a Google logo on the back.

There are plenty of third-party options that offer better protection, more useful features, or simply better value. I’ve picked six of the best Pixel 11 Pro Fold cases I’d consider, from slim, stylish options to rugged cases built for serious protection.

What to look for in a Pixel 11 Pro Fold case

A foldable phone changes the case-buying equation. With a conventional phone, you can get away with choosing based on drop protection and looks. With the Pixel 11 Pro Fold, that approach can get you a case that technically fits but makes the phone unpleasant to use.

Here’s what I’d prioritize.

  • Hinge protection: The hinge is one of the most important moving parts on a foldable, so I want a case that protects it without making opening and closing the phone awkward.
  • Fit the Fold snugly: A bulky case can turn an already substantial foldable into a brick, making it inconvenient to carry. If the case adds too much thickness, I’d rather go without it.
  • Grip is important: The Pixel 11 Pro Fold is a large, expensive device. A case that feels secure in one hand is worth more to me than a few extra millimeters of theoretical drop protection.
  • Magnetic compatibility is useful: The case should work well with Pixelsnap-style magnetic accessories such as chargers, stands, grips, and car mounts.
  • Protection should match your lifestyle: I don’t prefer a tank-like, rugged case since my phone spends most of its time on a desk. Likewise, an ultra-thin case isn’t the right choice if you regularly drop your phone.
  • Case material and finish: Clear TPU is practical, leather gets character over time, aramid fiber keeps things extremely light, and rugged polycarbonate/TPU constructions make more sense for accident-prone users.

The right Pixel 11 Pro Fold case is the one you’ll actually enjoy using every day, not the one with the longest feature list.

Why I’d skip Google’s official Pixelsnap case

Google’s official Pixel 11 Pro Fold case isn’t bad. That’s precisely why I think the alternatives are more interesting.

Google has improved its foldable case game this year. The official Pro Fold case features a color-matched soft silicone finish with subtle grip and inner microfiber lining for drop protection. But it also costs around $80, which puts it firmly into premium-case territory. At that price, I expect more than “it fits perfectly.”

I want a case that gives me a compelling reason to choose it over the alternatives. For some people, Google’s first-party fit and Pixelsnap integration will be enough. For everyone else, there are cases that offer a more distinctive combination of protection, materials, functionality, or value.

Overall, first-party doesn’t automatically mean best. Google makes good phones, but that doesn’t imply Google makes the best case I’d personally buy.

Top 6 cases I’d buy for Pixel 11 Pro Fold

1. ZAGG Crystal Palace Snap Lite: The clear case I’d actually consider

If you bought the Pixel 11 Pro Fold because you like how it looks, a clear case makes obvious sense. The problem is that cheap clear cases tend to become yellow, scratched, and grimy-looking surprisingly quickly.

That’s where ZAGG’s Crystal Palace is a perfect choice. This clear case for the Pixel 11 Pro Fold uses anti-yellowing technology, an anti-scratch finish, magnetic accessory compatibility, and an ultra-slim construction. It’s designed to disappear around the phone while still adding meaningful everyday protection.

Pros

  • Clear design keeps the Pixel 11 Pro Fold’s finish visible
  • Slim, lightweight approach
  • Magnetic accessory compatibility
  • Lifetime replacement policy from ZAGG

Cons

  • Still expensive for a clear case
  • Clear cases show fingerprints and wear
  • Not the best choice for maximum drop protection

My take: If I wanted to show off the Pixel 11 Pro Fold’s design without going completely caseless, this would be one of my first choices.

Check out on Amazon

2. Spigen Slim Armor Pro MagFit: The sensible everyday pick

If I were buying one case for the Pixel 11 Pro Fold without overthinking it, the Spigen Slim Armor Pro MagFit would be near the top of my list. It strikes a balance between strong protection, strong magnetic support for PixelSnap and MagSafe accessories, and a slim design that doesn’t feel like I’ve wrapped an expensive phone in a suit of armor.

Spigen uses its patented spring hinge mechanism to automatically keep the Fold’s hinge enclosed. Instead of relying on a simple flap that can shift, its SecuLink technology uses heat-treated steel pins to interlock the case’s front and rear sections. For a foldable case, that kind of long-term structural stability is something I value more than a flashy design.

Protection is also handled sensibly. Spigen’s Air Cushion Technology adds extra impact protection around the corners, while raised edges keep the camera area from sitting directly against a table or other flat surface.

Pros

  • More substantial protection than a minimalist shell
  • Good everyday balance of bulk and durability
  • MagFit support for accessories and wireless charging
  • Strong value compared with premium first-party cases

Cons

  • Not the thinnest case here
  • More utilitarian-looking than leather or aramid cases
  • No color option except black

My take: This is the case I’d recommend to someone who says, “I don’t care about showing off the case; I just want my expensive foldable protected.”

Check out on Amazon

3. TORRO Leather Wallet Case with Stand: Carry your essentials with ease

In a professional setting, my choice would definitely be a leather case for the Pixel 11 Pro Fold. TORRO’s leather case earns its place by combining protection, a kickstand, and a card holder in one package. It’s a very different proposition from a slim shell, but for the right person, that extra bulk makes sense.

It uses top-grain US cowhide, a shock-absorbing TPU frame, a microfiber lining, and a magnetic clasp for secure drop protection. The feature I’d probably use most is the integrated stand. The case can hold the Fold horizontally for watching videos, whether the phone is closed or fully unfolded. There’s also a hidden magnet sitting in the back of the frame.

Of course, there’s a trade-off: this is not the case I’d buy if my only goal were keeping the Fold as thin and light as possible. TORRO is for someone who wants their case to become part of their everyday carry.

Pros

  • Premium top-grain leather
  • Three card slots plus cash compartment
  • Works in folded and unfolded modes
  • Turns the phone into a convenient daily carry

Cons

  • Less minimalist than the other picks
  • Folio design isn’t for everyone
  • Carrying cards in the case makes the phone thicker

My take: If you want one thing in your pocket instead of two, this is one of the most compelling Pixel 11 Pro Fold cases here.

Check out on Amazon

4. PITAKA Ultra Slim Case: For people who bought the Pixel 11 Pro Fold for its thinness

This is my pick for the minimalist. PITAKA’s Pixel 11 Pro Fold Edge Case uses woven aramid fiber, a material known for its extreme lightness and strength. I enjoy its non-slip grip and silky-smooth hand feel. Although it’s just 0.05 in thick and 0.73oz light, it has an amber magnetic film embedded for wireless charging and magnetic accessories.

There is an important caveat: this isn’t the case I’d choose if maximum drop protection is your overriding concern. PITAKA itself positions it around protection from scratches, daily wear, and fingerprints, and its minimalist construction doesn’t pretend to be a rugged full-body shell.

But that’s exactly why I like it. The Pixel 11 Pro Fold is already a sophisticated piece of hardware. If you’re trying to preserve that sleek, premium feeling instead of wrapping it in layers of rubber, this is the direction I’d take.

Pros

  • Extremely slim and lightweight
  • Premium texture with beautiful color options
  • Wireless charging and magnetic accessory support
  • Doesn’t overwhelm the Fold’s design

Cons

  • Expensive for a minimalist case
  • Less protective than rugged alternatives
  • Not a full-coverage tank

My take: If you constantly think, “Why did I buy a thin foldable just to put it in a giant case?” buy this one.

Check out on Amazon

5. FNTCASE Matte Translucent Case: The value pick

Not every good Pixel 11 Pro Fold case needs to cost $70 or $80. FNTCASE is the option I’d buy if my priority were getting sensible everyday protection without paying for premium materials. The matte, translucent finish looks good because it resists fingerprints, stains, and minor scratches, and avoids a glossy plastic feel.

The case keeps the form factor relatively slim while providing military-grade protection against drops up to 18 feet, using a rigid polycarbonate back, flexible TPU bumpers, and four built-in corner airbags. I also like that FNTCASE doesn’t ignore the hinge. The built-in hinge protector is designed to help protect it against scratches, impacts, and accidental shifts.

The magnetic system is one of its more interesting features. In everyday use, you can use magnetic accessories and Qi wireless charging. Overall, it’s an important combination for me: protection without turning the Pixel 11 Pro Fold into a bulky brick.

Pros

  • More understated than a glossy clear case
  • Budget-friendly positioning
  • Slim enough to remain easy to carry
  • Less visually distracting than rugged designs

Cons

  • Less premium materials than PITAKA or TORRO
  • Not as distinctive as the leather option
  • Long-term durability is harder to judge

My take: If you don’t want to spend flagship-case money, FNTCASE is worth a look before automatically buying Google’s official option.

Check out on Amazon

6. Poetic Rugged Pixel 11 Pro Fold Case: For accident-prone people

If you’ve dropped your phone more times than you care to admit, commute with it in a bag full of other objects, work outdoors, or simply have terrible luck around concrete, don’t buy the prettiest case on this list. Buy this Poetic rugged case that makes you feel better when your phone inevitably slips.

It uses a dual-layer construction with shock-absorbing materials and reinforced corner bumpers, giving the case a much more substantial feel. You get good drop protection, with extra attention paid to the areas I’d worry about most on a foldable. The Poetic case also comes with a built-in magnetic ring for MagSafe compatibility.

Then there’s the built-in kickstand. It folds flat when I’m not using it, but when I want to watch a video, make a video call, or play a game, I can prop the Fold up in landscape mode and go hands-free. The case even includes a built-in 9H tempered-glass screen protector. That’s a big deal for anyone who wants an all-in-one solution.

Pros

  • Rugged full-body design
  • Better suited to high-risk environments
  • The translucent back shows off the phone’s design
  • Practical for media viewing

Cons

  • Bulkiest option on this list
  • Adds weight
  • Overkill for careful users

My take: Don’t buy this because it looks cool. Buy it because you know exactly why you need it.

Check out on Amazon

Which Pixel 11 Pro Fold case should you buy?

Here’s how I’d break it down:

My personal shortlist would be PITAKA, Spigen, and TORRO because they represent three genuinely different ways to use the Pixel 11 Pro Fold.

PITAKA preserves the phone’s sleek character. Spigen is the sensible all-rounder. TORRO turns the Fold into more of an everyday-carry accessory. And if I specifically wanted a clear case, I’d look at ZAGG before Google’s option.

That’s ultimately what bothers me about Google’s case strategy: there are so many interesting ways to protect this phone that “official” isn’t a compelling argument by itself.

Protect your expensive foldable in style!

The Pixel 11 Pro Fold is too expensive to settle for a boring case just because Google made it. A good case should solve a problem. It should make the phone safer, grippier to hold, easier to carry, or more useful.

That’s why I wouldn’t automatically buy Google’s official Pixel 11 Pro Fold case. It may be the easiest choice, but it isn’t the only one worth considering. From the slim PITAKA and practical Spigen to the wallet-friendly TORRO and rugged Poetic, there are better options depending on how you use your phone.

The right case ultimately comes down to what matters most to you. So, which one did you like the most? Let me know in the comments below!

  • Best Google Pixel 10a cases

title.rendered: Apple launches Mac mini with M6 and M5 Pro, starting at $899

content.rendered:
Apple has launched a new Mac mini with M6 and M5 Pro, its first update to the compact desktop in nearly two years. Pre-orders are open now, and deliveries begin September 22.

The five-by-five-inch design has not changed. The meaningful upgrades are inside: faster chips, more AI hardware, Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6, 2.5Gb Ethernet, and storage Apple says is up to twice as fast.

M6 powers the base Mac mini

The entry model skips M5 and moves directly from M4 to M6. It has a 12-core CPU, 12-core GPU, Neural Accelerators in every GPU core, and Apple’s first Dual 16-core Neural Engine.

Apple claims up to 40 percent faster CPU performance, twice the graphics performance, and four times the AI performance of the M4 model in its test configurations. Those are Apple’s own benchmark figures, so real-world gains will depend on the app and workload.

The M6 model starts with 16GB of unified memory and 256GB of storage. Memory can be configured up to 32GB, with bandwidth reaching 170GB/s on higher-memory versions.

M5 Pro is the more capable option

The higher-end Mac mini uses M5 Pro rather than M6. The older generation number is a little confusing, but the Pro chip has far more headroom for sustained creative, development, and local AI work.

It starts with a 15-core CPU, 16-core GPU, 24GB of memory, and 512GB of storage. Buyers can configure it with up to an 18-core CPU, 20-core GPU, 64GB of memory, and 8TB of storage. Memory bandwidth is 307GB/s.

M5 Pro first appeared in Apple’s 2026 MacBook Pro lineup, and our Mac processor history shows how it fits into the broader Apple silicon range.

Connectivity gets a useful upgrade

Both models use Apple’s N1 networking chip and support Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6, and Thread. Wired Ethernet now runs at 2.5Gb by default, with 10Gb available as an option.

The front still has two USB-C ports and a headphone jack. On the back, the M6 model has three Thunderbolt 4 ports, while M5 Pro gets three Thunderbolt 5 ports. Both include HDMI and Ethernet.

The new Mac mini can drive up to three external displays. Apple also added genlock over USB-C for synchronizing a display with professional camera capture.

Pricing is $100 higher this time

Mac mini with M6 starts at $899 in the U.S., while the M5 Pro version starts at $1,699. Each base configuration costs $100 more than the M4 model it replaces.

That price increase stings, especially after months of Mac mini and Mac Studio shortages. At least the base model still includes 16GB of memory, though 256GB of storage is tight for a desktop starting close to $900.

Apple is taking pre-orders in 30 countries and regions. The new models reach customers, Apple Stores, and authorized resellers on September 22.

acceptedAnswer.text: No, you must purchase the Fortnite Override Battle Pass to get the Sonic skin as it isn't available in the Shop.

title.rendered: Apple Maps ads are now rolling out on iPhone in the US and Canada

content.rendered:
Apple Maps has started showing ads to users in the United States and Canada. Apple confirmed to 9to5Mac that the rollout began in recent days and will expand over the coming weeks.

This is the live launch of the program Apple announced earlier this year. It puts sponsored businesses inside the same parts of Maps people use to discover nearby places.

Ads appear before and after a search

Apple is using two placements. Before you search, an ad can appear at the top of Suggested Places. After you enter a query, a relevant sponsored listing can appear in the results.

The ads look similar to ordinary business listings, but Apple marks them with a small blue Ad badge. That label may be easy to miss at a glance, especially when the sponsored result otherwise matches the layout of a normal place card.

Earlier iOS 26.5 beta screens previewed the same placements. The difference now is that regular users are starting to see them outside the beta.

Apple says Maps ad data stays private

Apple’s official Maps ads policy says a user’s location and ad interactions are not connected to an Apple Account. The company also says personal data stays on the device and is not collected, stored, or shared with third parties.

Ads can still be chosen for relevance based on what a person is searching for and the context Maps has on the device. Apple’s pitch is that it can offer useful local ads without building an identity-linked advertising profile.

The company has also restricted several advertiser categories, including home service providers, cryptocurrency ATMs, and bail bond companies.

The rollout is still limited

Apple announced Maps ads for the U.S. and Canada on iPhone and iPad. The current confirmation focuses on the iPhone rollout, so some users may not see a sponsored listing yet.

Businesses can create Maps campaigns through Apple Business or Apple Ads. For users, there is no separate ad-free Maps tier. Sponsored listings are becoming part of the standard discovery and search experience.

mainEntity.name: 1. How many Sonic The Hedgehog character skins are available in Fortnite?

acceptedAnswer.text: At the time of writing, there are four different Sonic franchise characters up for grabs, namely Sonic, Dr Eggman, Knuckles, and Shadow.

mainEntity.name: 2. Can I get the Sonic the Hedgehog skin from the Item Shop?

title.rendered: WhatsApp upgrades account security with passwords and multiple passkeys

content.rendered:
WhatsApp has announced three account security upgrades: stronger two-step verification, support for multiple passkeys, and more information about unknown callers on Android.

The first two changes protect the login process. The third gives Android users more context before answering a WhatsApp call from a number they do not recognize.

Two-step verification is getting a real password

WhatsApp’s two-step verification has relied on a six-digit PIN. The app is upgrading that PIN to a longer password that can contain letters, numbers, and special characters.

This extra check helps protect an account even when someone gets its one-time login code. It is a worthwhile change because a short PIN such as 123456 is easy to guess, but users still need to choose a unique password and keep their recovery details current.

Our WhatsApp account security guide covers the other settings worth checking, including linked devices, encrypted backups, and group permissions.

One account can now have multiple passkeys

More than one billion people have set up a WhatsApp passkey, according to the company. A passkey lets you verify your account with Face ID, a fingerprint, or your device’s screen-lock code instead of typing a code or PIN.

WhatsApp now lets an account hold more than one passkey. This is meant for people who use the same account across both iOS and Android and need a passkey tied to each device ecosystem.

You can check the option under Settings > Account > Passkeys. The feature is separate from the two-step verification password, so using one does not make the other redundant.

Android shows more details for unknown callers

When a non-contact calls through WhatsApp on Android, the incoming-call screen can now show whether the number is from another country and whether you share any groups with that person.

Those clues can help flag an obvious scam, but a shared group is not proof that a caller is trustworthy. WhatsApp’s earlier Strict Account Settings can apply more restrictive protections for people at higher risk of targeted attacks.

The caller-context feature is Android-only for now. WhatsApp has not announced an iPhone date. iPhone users can still use WhatsApp Privacy Checkup to silence unknown callers and review who can contact them.

title.rendered: OpenAI’s Admin plugin lets ChatGPT Work and Codex manage teams

content.rendered:
OpenAI has launched an Admin plugin for ChatGPT Work and Codex that lets workspace admins inspect usage, manage access, and make supported account changes from a conversation.

The plugin puts routine Admin Console work inside ChatGPT. An admin can ask which teams are using the most credits, check why someone cannot access a model, approve a spending request, or update a group without jumping between settings and reports.

What the Admin plugin can do

The first release covers four common parts of workspace administration:

  • Review activity, adoption, and credit use across ChatGPT Work and Codex
  • Add or remove members and update groups
  • Check effective permissions and control access to features or models
  • Change usage limits and approve or deny spending requests

Admins can ask follow-up questions before taking action. For example, they could compare credit use across teams, create a chart for a monthly review, then adjust a limit after seeing the underlying data.

That fits the broader idea behind ChatGPT Work, which is meant to complete multi-step jobs across tools rather than return a single answer.

Existing permissions still apply

The plugin does not create a shortcut around workspace controls. OpenAI says it works within the admin’s existing role and permissions, while respecting workspace policies and approval requirements.

It also returns a structured result for each request, so admins can see whether an action completed and what changed. Actions with wider impact can be reviewed before the plugin applies them.

That permission model matters more here than it does for a read-only report. Removing a member or changing model access has real consequences, and a conversational interface should not make those changes invisible.

It can automate recurring admin work

OpenAI says the plugin can monitor recurring conditions and route requests to Slack or Microsoft Teams. A company could send pending credit requests to an authorized reviewer or automatically grant feature access when a request meets predefined rules.

The Admin plugin joins tools such as the recent Apple Messages plugin for ChatGPT on Mac, but it targets the people running the workspace rather than the members using it.

Workspace admins can enable the plugin in ChatGPT settings, then install it from the Plugins directory in ChatGPT Work on the web or desktop app. OpenAI has not published a plan-by-plan availability list in the announcement.

mainEntity.name: 1. How many Sonic The Hedgehog character skins are available in Fortnite?

acceptedAnswer.text: At the time of writing, there are four different Sonic franchise characters up for grabs, namely Sonic, Dr Eggman, Knuckles, and Shadow.

mainEntity.name: 2. Can I get the Sonic the Hedgehog skin from the Item Shop?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, you must purchase the Fortnite Override Battle Pass to get the Sonic skin as it isn't available in the Shop.

mainEntity.name: 3. Is Tails available in Fortnite?

acceptedAnswer.text: While Tails is not available in Fortnite as a skin, you can still unlock his sidekick version by purchasing the Battle Pass for Chapter 7 Season 4 and reaching Level 2.

title.rendered: Upcoming Apple Products in 2026: Full List of What to Expect

content.rendered:
Apple is gearing up for one of its busiest product years yet in 2026, with rumored launches across iPhones, Macs, iPads, Apple Watches, home devices, audio accessories, and entirely new product categories. Based on the latest leaks and expert reporting, here are all the upcoming Apple products expected throughout the year.

Table of Contents
  • Fall 2026: The Big Launch Window
    • iPhone 18 Pro & iPhone 18 Pro Max
    • Apple’s First Foldable iPhone: iPhone Ultra
    • Apple Watch Series 12 & Watch Ultra 4
  • Late 2026: Last But Not Least
    • iPad mini (OLED)
    • MacBook Pro (M6)
    • iMac (M6)
    • iPad 12th Generation with Apple Intelligence
    • Apple Home and Display Products
  • TBA 2026: Apple Devices That Could Appear
    • MacBook Ultra
    • AirPods Pro with Cameras
    • Apple Glasses / AR Wearables
    • AR and Security Devices
  • Why 2026 Matters for Apple

Fall 2026: The Big Launch Window

The year kicked off with a host of budget-friendly and refreshed devices, including AirPods Max 2, MacBook Neo, MacBook Pro M5 Pro & M5 Max, MacBook Air M5, iPad Air M4, iPhone 17e, Studio Display & Studio Display XDR, Mac mini M6 & M5 Pro, and Mac Studio M5 Max & M5 Ultra.

Like clockwork, Fall will be the busiest quarter, with several major products slated for September–October.

iPhone 18 Pro & iPhone 18 Pro Max

This year, Apple is rumored to shift gears and only launch the flagship duo, the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max, in the iconic September event. The iPhone 18 base model could launch in the spring of 2027.

  • A20 Pro chip with significantly faster performance and improved energy efficiency
  • Advanced camera system with a DSLR-style variable Aperture lens and
  • Under-display Face ID, smaller display hole, and refined design cues like a transparent backpanel.
  • C2 modem for faster connections
  • New fun colors, such as Purple, Burgundy, etc.

Apple’s First Foldable iPhone: iPhone Ultra

Perhaps the most talked-about device of 2026, iPhone Fold, Apple’s first foldable smartphone, is expected around September alongside the new iPhones. Rumors suggest:

  • A crease-free, wide 7.7-inch display that may look like an iPad
  • Thinner build than the iPhone Air
  • 5.3-inch outer display and a Touch ID power button instead of Face ID
  • Side-by-side multitasking like iPad with iOS 27
  • Industry-first 24MP under-display camera
  • 5,400mAH big battery

The best part is iPhone Fold may launch at $1,800, which will help in wide adaptation and market dominance.

Apple Watch Series 12 & Watch Ultra 4

Apple is expected to launch the Apple Watch Series 12 and Watch Ultra 4 in Fall 2026, continuing its pace of yearly wearable updates.

  • New, faster S11 chips for smoother performance
  • Enhanced health sensors (potentially advanced metrics like glucose monitoring)
  • Refined designs with longer battery life
  • Additional satellite features for the Apple Watch Ultra 4
  • Ceramic case option in Series 12

Late 2026: Last But Not Least

Here are the remaining products that may launch at the end of the year from October to December:

iPad mini (OLED)

The iPad mini may transition to an OLED display with A19 Pro or A20 Pro chips for enhanced visuals and performance. It may feature a water-resistant design and a vibration-based speaker system.

MacBook Pro (M6)

A redesigned MacBook Pro with M6 silicon and an OLED display, rumored to be thinner, lighter, and packed with next-gen features like cellular support, could arrive late in autumn.

iMac (M6)

Reports suggest Apple is preparing an updated 24-inch iMac with the new M6 chip for the autumn release cycle. However, it may not receive a major redesign and only introduce some new color options. A larger display or OLED version is reportedly still several years away.

iPad 12th Generation with Apple Intelligence

The Apple iPad 12th generation is expected to be Apple’s next entry-level tablet, bringing meaningful performance upgrades while keeping the familiar iPad design. Rumors suggest it will feature a powerful A18 chip, which could enable Apple Intelligence AI features, Stage Manager 2, Wi-Fi 7, improved multitasking, and smoother everyday performance.

The device is also expected to include around 8GB of RAM, making it better suited for productivity, creative apps, and advanced iPadOS features. While the overall design may remain similar to the current model, the new iPad could still offer a 11-inch Liquid Retina display, 12MP cameras, and Touch ID, along with improved efficiency.

Apple Home and Display Products

  • Apple Studio Display 2 with mini‑LED backlighting, ProMotion support (120Hz), Thunderbolt 5, and 5K resolution.
  • A new Apple TV 4K with A17 Pro chipset, built-in FaceTime camera, Wi-Fi 7, and 8GB RAM for Apple Intelligence, Siri AI support, and a updated Siri remote.
  • Home devices like HomePod mini 2 is also likely. It may have S9 chip or newer with Siri AI, mesh extender support, UWB 2.0, Wi-Fi 7, better sound tuning, and new colors.
  • HomePod Smart Display (or Apple Home Hub) may arrive with 7-inch display with magnetic dock or stand, built-in camera for FaceTime, A18 chip for Apple Intelligence, and Siri AI integration.

TBA 2026: Apple Devices That Could Appear

These products are strongly rumored but don’t yet have a clear launch quarter:

MacBook Ultra

Apple’s rumored MacBook Ultra could become the company’s most ambitious Mac laptop yet. Current design reports point to a thinner body, OLED display, and touchscreen support, potentially making it the first Mac with a touchscreen.

The laptop is also rumored to replace the familiar display notch with an iPhone-style Dynamic Island, while Apple could explore built-in cellular connectivity. Recent reports suggest the first model may use M5 Pro and M5 Max chips.

The MacBook Ultra is expected to sit above the MacBook Pro in Apple’s lineup and carry a premium price. Its launch window remains uncertain, with reports pointing to late 2026 or early 2027.

AirPods Pro with Cameras

AirPods Pro with on-device cameras for visual AI features and improved spatial intelligence are expected to debut in the year.

Apple is reportedly developing multiple versions of camera-equipped AirPods, including models identified by the codenames B790 and B798. A leaked video found in macOS Tahoe 26.7 appears to demonstrate the technology, showing a user looking at a book while Siri uses Visual Intelligence to recognize and remember it.

Apple Glasses / AR Wearables

Apple’s long-anticipated AR glasses may be unveiled, potentially late in 2026 or teased for a 2027 ship window.

AR and Security Devices

  • A first-party smart security camera and video doorbell with Face ID support.
  • Targeting a 2027 launch, Vision Air could serve as a lightweight and budget-friendly alternative to Vision Pro. It is expected to be ~40% lighter with a magnesium alloy or plastic frame and likely powered by an A-series chip.

Why 2026 Matters for Apple

Apple’s strategy in 2026 is shaping up to be more aggressive, category-expanding, and ecosystem-wide than in typical years. The combination of staple updates (like iPhones and Macs), breakthrough category bets (foldables, Apple Glasses, smart home hubs), and AI-oriented experiences places 2026 as a pivotal year for consumer hardware and Apple’s long-term vision.

Bookmark this article; we’ll keep it updated as more rumors and confirmations roll in. Got a favorite from the list? Let us know in the comments!

title.rendered: Mac Processor History: How Apple Transformed Computing

content.rendered:
When you think of a Mac today, you probably imagine a fast, powerful machine powered by Apple’s latest M6 chip. But Macs weren’t always this advanced. Their journey began in the 1980s with the Motorola 68K series—a much simpler processor. Over the years, Apple transitioned to PowerPC, then Intel, and finally, its own Apple Silicon chips.

In this article, we’ll explore how Mac processors have evolved over time. You’ll see how each new chip improved speed, graphics, and memory, shaping the powerful Macs we use today.

Table of Contents
  • 2020–Present: Apple Silicon
    • M6 Chip Family: M6
    • M5 Chip Family: M5, M5 Pro, M5 Max, and M5 Ultra
    • M4 Chip family: M4, M4 Pro, and M4 Max
    • M3 Chip Family: M3, M3 Pro, M3 Max, and M3 Ultra
    • M2 Chip Family: M2, M2 Pro, M2 Max, and M2 Ultra
    • M1 Chip family: M1, M1 Pro, M1 Max, and M1 Ultra
  • 2006-2020: Intel x86
  • 1994-2005: Power PC
  • 1984-1995: Motorola 68 K

2020–Present: Apple Silicon

On June 22, 2020, Apple CEO Tim Cook announced a two-year transition plan to move from Intel processors to Apple Silicon. The goal was to create an all-Apple ecosystem by replacing Intel’s x86-64 architecture with Apple’s native ARM64-based chips.

Staying true to its timeline, Apple introduced its first Apple-designed chip, M1, in November 2020. This was followed by more powerful M1 variants in 2021. Apple then launched the M2, M3, M4, M5, and M6 chipsets, further pushing the boundaries of performance.

Here’s a detailed table outlining the evolution of Mac processors, from the latest Apple M4 Max back to the M1:

M6 Chip Family: M6

M6 (August 2026)

Apple’s M6 is the company’s first chip built using a state-of-the-art 2-nanometer process, bringing major improvements in CPU, GPU, storage and AI performance. It features a 12-core CPU, delivering up to 40 percent faster CPU performance, and a 12-core GPU, with two additional cores compared with M4.

AI is one of the biggest focuses of M6. The chip features an all-new Dual 16-core Neural Engine, which Apple says delivers up to 2x faster performance than the previous generation. Combined with the Neural Accelerators in the GPU, M6 is built to handle local AI workloads and next-generation Apple Intelligence features more efficiently.

Memory and storage performance have also been upgraded. Mac mini with M6 starts with 16GB of unified memory, configurable up to 32GB, while memory bandwidth reaches up to 170GB/s. Apple also claims up to 2x faster storage compared with the previous generation.

M5 Chip Family: M5, M5 Pro, M5 Max, and M5 Ultra

M5 (October 2025)

The M5 is the base chip in the M5 family and is created using  TSMC’s third-generation 3-nanometer process for mainstream laptops and tablets. It’s the first Apple Silicon chip to feature a dedicated Neural Engine in the GPU core, focusing on AI-driven tasks.

The chip features a 10-core CPU made up of 6 performance and 4 efficiency cores and up to a 10-core GPU, which provides solid graphics performance for tasks like photo editing and light 3D work. You can also configure it up to 32 GB of unified memory.

In Geekbench Single-Core scores, the M5 base model outperforms the whole M4 series and has the highest scores of any Apple silicon chip. Overall, it delivers a strong balance of performance, efficiency, and affordability for most users.

M5 Pro (March 2026)

The M5 Pro is designed for professionals who need more processing power than the base M5. Apple has designed a new Fusion Architecture specifically for AI tasks in this chip. It includes an 18-core CPU (6 super and 12 performance cores), offering 30% faster processing of intensive workloads. Apple has stated it as “the world’s fastest single-core performance.”

The GPU can scale up to around 20 cores with a dedicated Neural Accelerator in each core, delivering much stronger graphics performance. One of the major improvements in the M5 Pro is higher memory bandwidth up to 307GBps and up to 64 GB of unified memory, enabling large projects and datasets to run smoothly without slowdowns.

M5 Max (March 2026)

The M5 Max sits at the top of the M5 chip lineup and is built for users who need maximum performance. It is targeted at professionals working in fields such as 3D rendering, medical imaging, advanced video production, machine learning, and large-scale creative projects.

This chip features the same high-performance CPU architecture as the M5 Pro but dramatically expands the GPU capabilities. The GPU can scale up to 40 cores, making it one of the most powerful graphics systems available in a laptop.

The M5 Max also offers up to 614GBps memory bandwidth and supports up to 128 GB of unified memory. So, it can run large professional projects efficiently without relying heavily on external storage.

M5 Ultra (August 2026)

Apple’s M5 Ultra, introduced in August 2026, is designed specifically for demanding professional workflows and advanced AI workloads. The biggest change is Apple’s move to a quad-die architecture using next-generation UltraFusion technology, giving M5 Ultra the scale needed for extreme CPU, GPU and AI workloads.

You can configure it with up to a 36-core CPU and 80-core GPU. For AI, Apple has added Neural Accelerators to the GPU for the first time on an Ultra chip, delivering up to 4.3x the peak AI compute performance of M3 Ultra. The chip also supports up to 512GB of unified memory and an enormous 1.2TB/s of memory bandwidth.

Apple says M5 Ultra delivers up to 1.3x faster multithreaded CPU performance and up to 1.8x faster graphics performance than M3 Ultra. These improvements target workloads such as 3D rendering, video production, software development, scientific computing and AI inference.

M4 Chip family: M4, M4 Pro, and M4 Max

Apple’s M4 chip family represents the latest advancements in silicon technology, delivering enhanced performance and efficiency across various devices. Each chip—M4, M4 Pro, and M4 Max—is designed to meet different user needs.

M4 (May 2024)

The standard M4 chip is built using second-generation 3-nanometer technology, enhancing power efficiency and performance. It features a 10-core CPU with four performance cores and six efficiency cores, delivering up to 1.8 times faster performance than the M1 chip.

The 10-core GPU provides graphics performance up to twice as fast as the M1, making tasks like photo editing and gaming smoother. The 16-core Neural Engine, capable of performing up to 38 trillion operations per second, significantly boosts AI-related tasks and features like Apple Intelligence.

M4 Pro (October 2024)

The M4 Pro chip is designed for users with more demanding workflows. It boasts a 14-core CPU, comprising ten performance cores and four efficiency cores, offering up to 1.9 times faster performance than the M1 Pro.

The GPU includes up to 20 cores, providing graphics performance twice that of the standard M4. This makes it ideal for professionals engaged in tasks like app development, video editing, and complex simulations.

M4 Max (October 2024)

The M4 Max chip is the most powerful in the M4 family, targeting users requiring extreme performance. It features a 14-core CPU with ten performance cores and four efficiency cores, similar to the M4 Pro.

However, its GPU scales up to 32 cores, delivering exceptional graphics capabilities suitable for high-end tasks such as 3D rendering and large-scale data processing. The M4 Max also supports higher unified memory bandwidth, enhancing data-intensive operations.

All M4 chips support advanced features like hardware-accelerated ray tracing and mesh shading, enhancing graphics rendering and gaming experiences. They also enable Thunderbolt 5 connectivity, offering faster data transfer speeds and improved peripheral support.

M3 Chip Family: M3, M3 Pro, M3 Max, and M3 Ultra

Apple’s M3 chipset family includes four powerful processors: M3, M3 Pro, M3 Max, and M3 Ultra. Each is designed to meet different performance needs, from everyday tasks to demanding professional workloads.​

M3 (October 2023)

The M3 chip is built using advanced 3-nanometer technology, making it faster and more efficient. It features an 8-core CPU with four performance cores and four efficiency cores, delivering up to 30% faster performance than the M1.

The 10-core GPU provides enhanced graphics performance, making tasks like photo editing and gaming smoother. The 16-core Neural Engine, capable of performing up to 15.8 trillion operations per second, significantly boosts AI-related tasks.

M3 Pro (October 2023)

The M3 Pro chip is designed for users with more demanding workflows. It boasts a 12-core CPU, comprising six performance cores and six efficiency cores, offering up to 40% faster performance than the M1 Pro.

The GPU features up to 18 cores, delivering graphics performance ideal for professionals in video editing, programming, and other demanding tasks. Apple has also integrated 37 billion transistors to enhance the overall performance of Mac machines.

M3 Max (October 2023)

The M3 Max chip is one of the most powerful in the M3 family, targeting users requiring extreme performance. It features a 14-core CPU with ten performance cores and four efficiency cores, similar to the M3 Pro.

However, its GPU scales up to 38 cores, delivering exceptional graphics capabilities suitable for high-end tasks such as 3D rendering and large-scale data processing. The M3 Max also has 92 billion transistors to enhance data-intensive operations.

M3 Ultra (March 2025)

The M3 Ultra chip is Apple’s most powerful processor to date. It features a 32-core CPU with 24 performance cores and eight efficiency cores, delivering up to 1.8 times the performance of the M1 Ultra.

Its GPU includes up to 80 cores, providing up to 2.6 times faster graphics performance than the M1 Ultra. The M3 Ultra also supports up to 512GB of unified memory—the highest ever in a personal computer—making it ideal for tasks like visual effects and AI development.

M2 Chip Family: M2, M2 Pro, M2 Max, and M2 Ultra

M2 (June 2022)

The M2 processor in the MacBook houses an 8-core CPU with a configuration of 4 performance cores and 4 efficiency cores. Apple claims that M2’s CPU gives twice the performance of the latest 10-core PC laptop processor.   

In addition, the M2 processor offers unparalleled work performance with an 8—or 10-core GPU, 16-core neural engine, and 100GBps bandwidth. M2 chips have different RAM variations: 8GB, 16GB, and 24 GB. 

M2 Pro (January 2023) 

M2 Pro has a robust 10-core or 12-core CPU, including 6 or 8 performance and 2 efficiency cores. Like the M1 Pro, the M2 Pro has an inbuilt media engine that accelerates H.264, HEVC, and ProRes video encoding and decoding. Besides, the chip provides improved power efficiency when playing 4K and 8K ProRes streams thanks to the 16- or 19-core GPU.

Further, the M2 Pro has a 16-core neural engine, 200 GBps memory bandwidth, and 16 GB or 32 GB RAM variants. Apple claimed the M2 Pro offered exceptional image processing capabilities. However, it is only equipped with a MacBook Pro to handle its high efficiency.   

M2 Max (January 2023) 

M2 Max added another layer of efficiency to the Apple Silicon range. Its core specifications included a 12-core CPU with 8 performance and 4 efficiency cores. Like its predecessor, the M2 Max comes with two ProRes and video-encoding engines.   

Regarding graphics, it supports a 30- or 38-core GPU to give you the most detailed output. While the GPU support is better than M1 Max, the 16-core neural engine remains the same for both variants. In addition, Apple introduced the chip in 3 RAM variants- 32 GB, 64 GB, and 96 GB.   

Moreover, Apple asserted that the M2 Max was 30% better than the M1 version when using color grading in DaVinci Resolve. It also offers 400 GB of memory bandwidth, ensuring quick processing.   

M2 Ultra (June 2023) 

At the recent WWDC 2023, Apple launched its most efficient iteration of the Apple Silicon series: M2 Ultra. It offers the power of two M2 Max chips interwoven using the robust UltraFusion architecture. Regarding specifications, M2 Ultra features a 24-core CPU and a maximum of 76-core GPU support.

It also carries 134 billion transistors, up to 192GB of unified memory, and an impressive 800 GB of memory bandwidth. You can experience this beast in the latest Mac Studio and Mac Pro. According to Apple, Mac Studio with M2 Ultra is 3x faster than its earlier version.

Besides, it can run 22 streams of 8K ProRes video together. The M2 Ultra chip enables the Mac Pro to deliver 3D simulations and video transcoding up to 3x faster. Moreover, the processor can simultaneously consume 24 inputs from 4K cameras and encode them to ProRes. 

M1 Chip family: M1, M1 Pro, M1 Max, and M1 Ultra

M1 (November 2020)

The M1 processor was Apple’s first venture into chip design for the Mac. Indeed, it was a big blow for Intel! Regarding specs, M1 chips offer an 8-core CPU with 4 performance and 4 efficiency cores and a 7- or 8-core GPU support.

Besides, the 16-core Neural Engine embedded in the M1 series accelerates and optimizes machine learning operations on Mac. In addition, the chip offered 68.25 GB of memory bandwidth. However, it only supported two RAM variations—8GB and 16GB. The small storage capacity didn’t go down well with many Mac users.  

M1 Pro (October 2021)

Next in line in the M1 series was M1 Pro. This chipset supported 8-or-10-core CPUs, configured as 6 or 8 performance and 2 efficiency cores. Besides, Apple included a 14-or-16-core GPU, which is 2x faster than M1. Also, the new GPU was up to 7x more quickly than the integrated graphics on the 8-core laptop chip.

Besides, it featured a ProRes accelerator in the media engine for faster video processing. Its memory bandwidth of up to 200 GB is nearly 3x better than the M1. This time, Apple expanded its storage capacity with M2, introducing 16GB and 32GB chips. 

M1 Max (October 2021)

The M1 Max and M1 Pro chips were launched together. They had a 10-core CPU with 8 performance and 2 efficiency cores, a 24- or 32-core GPU, and a 16-core Neural Engine. The graphics performance of the 32GB GPU is up to 4x faster than that of the M1 chip.   

Its two ProRes accelerators can deliver up to 2x faster video encoding than M1 Pro. Moreover, the processor offers up to 400 GB of memory bandwidth, two times more than the M1 Pro and 6x improved than the M1. Besides, the 64GB RAM adds some extra credit points.   

Apple introduced the M1 Max chip only for the MacBook Pro and Mac Studio.   

M1 Ultra (March 2022)

The M1 Ultra was launched as a standard option for the Mac Studio. This powerful processor has UltraFusion architecture connecting the two M1 Max chips. It houses a 20-core CPU with 16 performance and 4 efficiency cores. For graphics, Apple added a massive 48- or 64-core GPU support.

So, you get improved latency, reduced bandwidth, and better power consumption. Furthermore, the chip has up to 128GB of unified memory built, offering twice the media engine performance of the M1 Max.   

2006-2020: Intel x86

At WWDC 2005, Apple announced its transition to Intel chips, and the first Intel Macs were announced in early 2006. These included an iMac and the MacBook Pro, which boasted almost four-fold enhanced performance from their predecessors. 

Further, from Mac OS X 10.4.4, Apple included an advanced emulation technology called Rosetta. It helped maintain software compatibility between generations. Soon, Apple introduced programs with universal binaries that could run on both PowerPC and Intel Macs.

As the transition to x86 eventually came a full circle, Rosetta was removed from Mac OS X 10.7 Lion going forward. So far, about 80 Mac models have featured Intel CPUs. This changed with the introduction of ARM-based Macs.

1994-2005: Power PC

In the late 1980s, new trends began taking over the computing industry, overshadowing the legacy CPU architectures. Apple partnered with IBM and Motorola to design a common CPU platform that could rival the “Wintel” (Microsoft-Intel) domination. 

The Power Macintosh 6100 used the PowerPC architecture, following which around 87 different Mac models were launched. Clock speeds increased from 60 MHz to 2.7 GHz, which was remarkable for that era. The final Apple PowerPC model was released in November 2005. 

1984-1995: Motorola 68 K 

The 1984 Apple Macintosh computer had an 8 MHz Motorola 68000 CPU. While in development, an early Mac prototype used an 8/16-bit Motorola 6809 CPU. But after a designer noticed the impressive graphics routines that were being created for the 68000-based Apple Lisa, the more expensive 16/32-bit 68000 was chosen. 

While the Apple Lisa used only a 5 MHz 68000, the new Mac prototype could run at 8 MHz. This appealed to Steve Jobs, who was eager to upstage the Lisa team. 

Over the following decade, every Macintosh used successors of the 68000, including the pure 32-bit 68020, 68030, and 68040 chips. These got faster and more complex over time. Overall, at least 72 different Macs used 68k CPUs, the last of which was the PowerBook 190 in 1995. 

The best is yet to come! 

The history of Apple processors beautifully captures the tech giant’s true ideology. The Mac has witnessed everything from laptop size to its architecture. I hope you enjoyed reading this article as much as we enjoyed traveling the Mac timeline while penning it.

Please share your reviews in the comments section. Till then, enjoy reading.  

FAQs

The oldest Mac software is Mac OS X Server 1.0.

What is the full form of Mac?

The complete form of the Mac is Macintosh.

mainEntity.name: 1. How many Sonic The Hedgehog character skins are available in Fortnite?

acceptedAnswer.text: At the time of writing, there are four different Sonic franchise characters up for grabs, namely Sonic, Dr Eggman, Knuckles, and Shadow.

mainEntity.name: 2. Can I get the Sonic the Hedgehog skin from the Item Shop?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, you must purchase the Fortnite Override Battle Pass to get the Sonic skin as it isn't available in the Shop.

mainEntity.name: 3. Is Tails available in Fortnite?

acceptedAnswer.text: While Tails is not available in Fortnite as a skin, you can still unlock his sidekick version by purchasing the Battle Pass for Chapter 7 Season 4 and reaching Level 2.

title.rendered: I changed these Windows Search settings, and finding files got much easier

content.rendered:
Windows Search is useful out of the box, but it seems inefficient in certain situations. If I couldn’t remember the exact filename, I would go to the search bar, try a few variations, and eventually wonder why finding a document on my own PC felt so hard.

The problem wasn’t really Windows Search. It was how Windows was indexing my files. Once I customized a handful of Windows Search indexing settings, search became much more predictable. If you also want to improve Windows Search in Windows 11 to find files faster, here are the best settings you should change right now.

Why Windows Search can feel inefficient

Windows Search relies heavily on a system called the index: a catalog of file names, paths, properties, and, when configured to do so, the text inside files. Instead of scanning each drive on your PC every time you search, Windows can simply use the index to provide you with the necessary results quickly.

That sounds simple, but there is an obvious catch: Windows can only search efficiently for what it has actually indexed.

By default, Windows 11’s Classic search mode indexes common locations such as Documents, Pictures, Music, and the Desktop. You need to enable Enhanced Search to index the entire PC, but Microsoft notes that this can consume more system resources.

That explains a lot of the “Windows Search is broken” complaints I’ve had. Sometimes the file wasn’t missing. Search simply wasn’t looking in the folder where I’d saved it. And sometimes the file was indexed, but Windows only knew about its properties, not the words inside it. So instead of accepting Windows Search as-is, I started optimizing it to search files faster.

5 tips that improved my Windows search

1. Making Windows index the folders I actually use

This was the first change I made, and arguably the most important. I organize my files differently from the way Windows expects me to do it. Some folders that I need to access regularly are not located in the standard Documents folder, and that’s where the search problem started.

If Windows doesn’t index a location, using the Search bar won’t necessarily give you the fast, reliable results you expect.

In Windows 11, follow these steps:

  1. Launch Settings on your PC.
  2. Click Privacy & security on the left sidebar. Now, scroll and select Search.
  3. Under Find my files, choose Enhanced search.
  4. Now, Windows will scan and index the entire PC. Keep it plugged in to finish the process, as it will take some time.

You can also customize which locations are indexed and exclude unimportant folders to speed up the process. Click Add an excluded file and select temporary folders, old archives, development files, large collections of documents you never search, and application data.

But I like to be more methodical about it: index the folders I actually search, rather than blindly indexing everything. If you have a dedicated work folder, downloads directory, or external folder and want to save resources, keep the Search settings set to Classic and add the drive or folder to your indexed locations.

Simply click Customize search location under Classic > Modify in the dialog box, then choose a drive or a specific folder. Click Ok to save the location. That’s much more useful than assuming every folder on my PC is important.

One important caveat: indexing can take time initially. Microsoft says the first indexing pass can take up to a couple of hours, depending on the amount of data. After that, Windows updates the index as files change.

2. I enabled file-content searching for the documents I need

This setting made Windows Search feel dramatically smarter. Searching by filename is useful when you remember the filename. However, most of the time I forget the name and usually remember something inside the file.

For example, you may remember that a document mentioned “Q4 budget,” “client onboarding,” or “backup strategy,” but you can’t be sure about its name. In such cases, enable Windows to index file contents along with the default file names and properties.

  1. Go to Settings > Privacy & security > Search.
  2. Scroll down and click Advanced indexing options.
  3. It will open the indexing options control panel. Here, click Advanced at the bottom. Ensure you have administrative access.
  4. Move to the File Types tab. Select Index Properties & File Contents.
  5. Click Ok to apply the changes.
  6. Now, search for a sentence or keywords, and the Search bar will actually pull up documents containing them.

Content indexing makes the search index more useful, but it can also make the index larger. For me, searchable documents are worth it. That’s why I deselected the file types I don’t usually use and then enabled content indexing to minimize the process load.

If you regularly search PDFs, Word documents, text files, spreadsheets, or similar files by words contained inside them, this is one of the first settings I’d check.

And on supported Copilot+ PCs, Windows 11 can go beyond traditional keyword indexing with semantic indexing, which is designed to surface results based on the meaning of a query rather than matching only exact terms.

3. Clean up search results with better filters

Sometimes Windows Search isn’t failing. You’re just asking it a question that’s too vague. I learned to use search terms that give Windows more context, rather than typing a single generic word and scrolling through a mountain of results.

If you’re looking for a spreadsheet about a particular project, search using several useful terms rather than just the project name.

Instead of searching report“, try narrowing it with a search operator at the end like report kind:document datemodified:last week. Now, Windows will find the document file type named report that you accessed last week. If you type “size:>10MB, the search result returns files sized more than 10 MB.

You can also use multiple search operators together or access the search options to find files faster by file type, date, name, and other properties.

  1. Open File Explorer and click the search bar in the top-right corner.
  2. Enter the file name or keyword.
  3. Now, select Search options. Here, you will find different filters.

The less irrelevant material Windows has to return, the less time you spend scanning the results.

4. Use filename extensions when you know the format

If you know you’re looking for a PDF, don’t make Windows sift through Word documents, spreadsheets, images, and everything else.

For example: *.pdf Or combine the extension with a keyword: budget *.pdf

Likewise:

  • *.docx
  • *.xlsx
  • *.pptx

This is particularly useful when several files have similar names.

Moreover, when I know the file is somewhere inside Documents\Projects I open that folder first and search there. Don’t search the entire PC to get faster results.

5. Rebuild the Search Index when the search is broken

This is the nuclear option, but sometimes it’s exactly what you need.

If Windows Search suddenly stops finding files that it previously found, returns obviously incomplete results, or behaves inconsistently even after you’ve checked your indexed locations and file types, it may be time to take care of the Search index itself.

Windows 11 lets you rebuild the index to troubleshoot search problems.

  1. Go to Search settings in Privacy & security.
  2. Click Advanced indexing options and select Advanced at the bottom.
  3. Finally, click Rebuild.

Now, Windows will remove the old index, crawl your entire PC according to your configuration, and create a new search directory. It gives Windows a fresh catalog to work from. However, remember that rebuilding doesn’t automatically mean that your files will become more searchable.

And yes, the process can take hours to complete and bump your CPU usage. That’s why I wouldn’t rebuild the index every time Search feels slightly slow. Check your indexing settings and rebuild only when the index itself appears to be the problem.

What I wouldn’t change

I’m deliberately not recommending that everyone turn on every search option.

Indexing more locations can increase the amount of data Windows has to catalog. Searching the entire PC can also have resource implications. If you have a relatively clean file structure and rarely search outside your normal user folders, Classic search may be perfectly adequate.

I also wouldn’t enable content indexing for every obscure file type simply because the option exists. My approach is more practical:

  • Index what I use.
  • Make the important documents searchable by content.
  • Exclude what I never search.
  • Ensure specific file types are selected in search settings.

That’s enough.

Final takeaway

Windows Search doesn’t need a dramatic overhaul. It needs a little direction.

The biggest improvement I made was realizing that the search box doesn’t determine what Windows can find. The search index, indexed locations, file types, and search scope determine what information Windows has available when I ask it a question.

Once you change those settings around the way you actually store and search for files, Windows Search finds files way faster.

In case you missed:

  • Windows was reserving my RAM. Here’s how I got my usable memory back
  • How to screen record on Windows
  • The Windows Clipboard shortcut I wish I started using years ago
