title.rendered: I moved my Android data to an iPhone: Here’s the transfer method I’d use again

content.rendered:
I’ll be honest: moving from Android to iPhone used to be the part of the switch I dreaded most. The iPhone itself is easy to set up. The headache is everything sitting on the old Android phone, including thousands of photos, years of WhatsApp conversations, contacts, messages, files, and the phone number you don’t want to lose.

In 2026, however, this issue is much less troublesome. Apple still recommends Move to iOS, but there is now another option: compatible Android phones running Android 17 or later can transfer data to an iPhone without installing the Move to iOS app. Apple also supports a direct USB-C connection for faster transfers.

Here’s exactly how I move data from Android to iPhone.

What can you transfer from Android to iPhone?

Before starting, it helps to know what Apple can actually move. Otherwise, you may finish the transfer and wonder where your music collection or PDF files went.

Apple says the supported transfer can include:

  • Contacts
  • Message history
  • SMS messages
  • Call history
  • Camera photos and videos
  • Photo albums
  • Files and folders
  • Accessibility settings
  • Display settings
  • Web bookmarks
  • Mail accounts
  • WhatsApp messages and media
  • Voice Memos
  • Calendars
  • Some free apps that are available on both Google Play and the App Store and support the transfer feature

That covers most of the data I would consider important when changing phones. But there are some notable exceptions.

What doesn’t automatically transfer?

Apple specifically says music, books, and PDFs need to be moved manually. Apps that aren’t available on the App Store also won’t magically appear on your iPhone.

So don’t think of this as cloning your Android phone onto an iPhone. It’s better to think of it as moving the supported data into Apple’s ecosystem and then rebuilding the rest.

Before you transfer data from Android to iPhone

This is the part I wouldn’t rush.

Apple recommends turning on Wi-Fi and plugging both phones into power before beginning. You should also make sure everything you’re transferring, including data stored on an external Micro SD card, will fit on the new iPhone.

I would check these things first:

  • Charge both phones.
  • Plug both phones into power.
  • Turn on Wi-Fi on Android.
  • Check the available storage on your iPhone.
  • Check how much data is actually stored on Android.
  • Include Micro SD card content in your storage calculation.
  • Update Chrome on Android to transfer Chrome bookmarks.
  • Keep your USB-C cable nearby if you want to try a wired transfer.

Tip: If WhatsApp contains years of photos and videos, don’t underestimate how much space it can consume.

Should you use a USB-C cable to transfer Android data to an iPhone?

Yes, if you have a compatible cable.

Apple says you can directly connect an Android phone and an iPhone with a USB-C cable for faster transfer. That’s my preferred approach when moving a large amount of data.

A wireless transfer is convenient, but when you’re moving years of photos, videos, and messages, I would rather have the two phones physically connected than depend entirely on a wireless connection.

One small warning: Apple notes that when you connect the phones by cable, Android may show a USB-related pop-up, and you might need to adjust the USB settings before Move to iOS can start.

Method 1: Transfer data from Android to iPhone with Move to iOS

This remains the most universal official method. If your Android device does not support Apple’s new app-free transfer system, then this is how I’d do it.

Step 1: Start setting up your iPhone

Turn on the new iPhone and place it near your Android phone, and follow the setup instructions.

  1. On the Quick Start screen, choose Set Up Without Another Device and continue.
  2. Eventually, you’ll reach the Transfer Your Apps & Data screen.
  3. Then tap From Android and select Transfer with App.

Note: If you’ve already completed iPhone setup, you need to erase the iPhone and start again to use Move to iOS. If you don’t want to erase it, you’ll need to move your content manually instead.

Step 2: Open Move to iOS on Android

On your Android phone, open the Move to iOS app.

I didn’t have it installed. But don’t worry, Apple provides a QR code shortcut on the new iPhone that takes you to the Google Play download page.

Once downloaded, launch the Move to iOS app and follow the next steps:

  1. Tap Continue.
  2. Read and accept Apple’s terms.
  3. Choose whether to automatically send app data to Apple. I selected Automatically Send to share app data seamlessly.
  4. Tap Continue to move through the permission prompts.
  5. Allow Location and Notifications permissions when requested.

If you’re using a USB-C cable, you may also see a USB settings prompt.

Step 3: Enter the transfer code

On your iPhone, tap Continue when you reach the Move from Android screen. The iPhone will display a six-digit or ten-digit code.

Enter that code into the Android phone. The iPhone essentially creates a temporary connection so the two phones can communicate.

Step 4: Connect Android to the iPhone’s temporary Wi-Fi network

The iPhone creates a temporary Wi-Fi network.

When Android asks whether you want to join it, tap Connect.

Wait for the Transfer Data screen to appear.

If Android displays a warning about a weak internet connection, don’t panic. Apple specifically says you can ignore that alert during this process.

Step 5: Choose what you want to transfer

Now you’ll see the data that can be moved.

Select what you want to transfer and tap Continue. I have already shared the data types you can move from Android and iPhone.

Now, leave both phones alone until the iPhone’s loading bar finishes.

Even if the Android phone says the transfer is complete, I always wait until the progress bar on the iPhone has finished. Keep the phones close together and plugged in.

I would not:

  • Open another Android app
  • Answer a phone call
  • Turn off the screen unnecessarily
  • Walk away with one phone
  • Disconnect the Wi-Fi
  • Restart either phone

Apple specifically warns that using another app or receiving a call on Android before the transfer finishes can prevent the content from transferring.

Step 6: Complete the setup

Once the progress bar completes, tap Done on your Android device.

Also, tap Continue on your iOS device and follow the on-screen instructions to sign in to your Apple Account and continue setting up your device.

You can activate your phone number and SIM or eSIM on the iPhone during the move. Depending on your carrier, you may be directed to the carrier’s website to complete activation.

Method 2: Transfer data from Android to iPhone without the app

Apple has upgraded the Move to iOS app to make the transfer seamless.

If you have a supported Android device running a compatible version of Android 17 or later, you can transfer data without installing Move to iOS. Device-manufacturer support is required, so Android 17 alone doesn’t guarantee that every phone supports the feature.

If your phone supports it, I’d choose this method first.

How does transfer without Move to iOS app work

On the new iPhone:

  1. Begin iPhone setup.
  2. Go to Transfer Your Apps & Data.
  3. Tap From Android and select Transfer without App.
  4. Place the Android phone next to the iPhone.
  5. Tap Continue.
  6. Your iPhone will show a QR code to establish a connection. Use the Android camera to scan it.
  7. Select the data you want to transfer to your Android. It includes photos, contacts, calendars, call history, and messages.
  8. Wait for the transfer to finish.
  9. Tap Continue on the iPhone.

The process is as simple as that. Check if everything has been moved successfully before factory resetting your Android.

The best part is that I can quickly transfer my eSIM to the new iPhone with the app-free method. After the data transfer, select the phone number on your Android device and tap Transfer. Once the eSIM transfer is complete, continue setting up the iPhone.

However, this depends on the device and carrier, so I wouldn’t assume every Android-to-iPhone switch will have a one-tap eSIM experience. You may need to manually activate the number in that case.

What if the QR code won’t scan?

You aren’t stuck. Apple provides a manual pairing method for the app-free transfer.

On the iPhone, when the QR code appears, tap Other Options.

Then on Android, follow these steps:

  1. Go to Settings and select Google Services.
  2. Tap All Services and select Pair with iPhone or iPad > Copy Data.
  3. Now, type the session ID and pairing code shown on your iPhone or iPad and tap Continue.
  4. Wait for the transfer to complete on your iPhone or iPad.

Note: If your Android phone doesn’t provide a place to enter the session ID and pairing code, you may need to contact the device manufacturer.

How to transfer WhatsApp from Android to iPhone

For many Android users, this is the part that matters most.

The good news is that Apple’s Move to iOS process supports transferring WhatsApp messages and media. When you reach the content-selection screen during the transfer, make sure WhatsApp data is included.

After the transfer finishes, I recommend opening WhatsApp on the iPhone and checking:

  • Recent conversations
  • Older conversations
  • Photos
  • Videos
  • Group chats
  • Important attachments

Don’t wipe the Android phone immediately. I would keep the old phone untouched until I’ve checked the data I care about most.

What happens to your Android Apps?

This is where Android-to-iPhone migration behaves differently from moving between two Android phones. Your Android apps don’t simply get copied to iOS.

As per my testing, when a free app is available on both Google Play and the App Store and supports the transfer feature, it moves to iPhone smoothly. Once the transfer is finished, you can download those matched apps from the App Store.

For everything else, you need to open the App Store, download the iPhone version manually, and sign back in.

And if an Android app isn’t available for iPhone, you’ll need to find an alternative.

How to transfer music, books, and PDFs

This is where I think Apple’s automatic transfer deserves an asterisk.

It doesn’t move everything. You need to send music, books, and PDFs manually.

  • For music: If you use a streaming service, the easiest option is simply to install its iPhone app from the App Store and sign in. The same applies to Apple Music—just sign in with your account.
  • Transfer Books and PDFs: For Kindle, Nook, Google Play Books, and similar services, install the corresponding iPhone app and sign in to access your library.
  • Move files: For documents stored in cloud services such as Google Drive, Dropbox, or OneDrive, install the relevant service’s iPhone app and sign in.

For files, PDFs, and ePub books stored locally, you can use a computer as an intermediate step. Connect your Android phone to a computer and copy the files from the Documents folder. Then connect your iPhone and, on Mac, drag them into the Books app or sync via Finder. On Windows, use the Apple Devices app to sync them.

What if I’ve already set up my iPhone?

Here’s the catch that can save you a lot of frustration: Move to iOS is designed to work during iPhone setup.

If you’ve already finished setting up the iPhone, you need to erase the iPhone and start over to use the Move to iOS transfer. If you don’t want to erase the iPhone, you’ll have to manually move the content, contacts, text messages, call history, and more.

My advice is simple: Don’t spend an hour customizing a brand-new iPhone before deciding how you’re going to transfer your Android data. Choose your transfer method first.

Android-to-iPhone transfer not working? Try these fixes

Move to iOS is convenient, but it isn’t immune to problems. If the transfer fails, I’d go through these fixes in this order. From checking your connection and restarting both phones to ensuring enough storage and updating the software, these simple steps can often get the transfer working again.

1. Keep Move to iOS open

Don’t switch apps on Android, answer calls or let another process interrupt the transfer.

Apple specifically says the Move to iOS app should remain on screen until the transfer finishes.

2. Turn off mobile data

I recommend turning off the Android phone’s cellular data connection, as it might have an unstable speed, and trying the transfer again if you’re having problems.

3. Disable Wi-Fi features that interfere

Some Android phones have features that automatically switch networks or optimize connections.

Apple specifically mentions settings such as Smart Network Switch and Sprint Connections Optimizer as examples of settings that can interfere with the transfer.

4. Forget saved Wi-Fi networks

If your internet connection is still slow or experiencing hiccups, forget the connected Wi-Fi network on your Android device, reconnect to it, and try one more time.

5. Restart both phones

It’s boring advice, but I trust it the most. It removes the cache and refreshes the system.

Restart the Android and iPhone, then start the transfer again. Apple lists restarting both devices among its recommended troubleshooting steps.

What if your iPhone runs out of storage?

This is the problem I would take seriously before starting the transfer.

Sometimes, you may end up with only some content transferred, as the iPhone may appear full even though the transfer didn’t actually finish. In that situation, erase the iPhone, restart the transfer, and select content that fits within the iPhone’s available storage.

So check storage first. If your Android phone has 180GB of photos, videos, and files, moving to a 128GB iPhone won’t magically solve the math.

Switch from Android to iPhone easily!

Switching from Android to iPhone doesn’t have to be complicated. With Move to iOS, Apple’s new Transfer without App option for supported Android 17+ devices, and USB-C transfers, I can move most of my important data without starting from scratch.

I’d recommend checking my storage first, keeping both phones plugged in, and making sure my photos, contacts, messages, WhatsApp chats, and eSIM have transferred successfully. Music, books, and PDFs may still need to be moved manually.

Once everything looks good, you can finally say goodbye to your old Android phone and enjoy your new iPhone without worrying about leaving important data behind.

keyPoints.title: Backup and Charge Before Transfer
keyPoints.explanation: Ensure your Android device is backed up and both devices are sufficiently charged before starting the data transfer process.

keyPoints.title: Using Move to iOS App for Initial Setup
keyPoints.explanation: The Move to iOS app helps transfer data during the initial setup of your new iPhone, but isn't usable after setup is complete.

keyPoints.title: Alternative Methods for Data Transfer
keyPoints.explanation: You can transfer data after setup by syncing your Google account or using third-party software like iToolLab or PhoneTrans for more comprehensive data migration.

keyPoints.title: Transferring Data with Google Account
keyPoints.explanation: Backing up data to your Google account allows easy syncing of contacts, photos, and documents to your iPhone via Google services like Google Drive and Google Photos.

keyPoints.title: Third-party Software for Complete Transfer
keyPoints.explanation: Third-party tools like iToolLab and PhoneTrans can facilitate full data transfer, including WhatsApp chats, when Move to iOS isn't sufficient or available.

title.rendered: How to get Addison Rae skin in Fortnite

content.rendered:
For a long time, Epic Games has been expanding its catalog of Fortnite celeb skins by collaborating with some of the biggest and most popular names in the music industry. The latest name to be put on the list is that of the American singer Addison Rae, whose in-game cosmetics recently arrived in the Item Shop.

There are two different Addison Rae skins currently available, namely Famous Addison Rae and Addison Rae. While the former is worth 1,800 V-Bucks, the latter comes in at 1,500 V-Bucks. Both these skins and associated cosmetics are up for grabs only until August 16 at 5 PM PT or 8 PM ET. Below, you can find the steps to follow for claiming your desired Addison Rae Fortnite skin.

Steps to get the Addison Rae skin in Fortnite

  1. In Fortnite, navigate to the Shop tab.
  2. Then, scroll to the Addison Rae section and select your desired skin.
  3. Finally, select and hold the Purchase button to confirm your choice.

For those who are looking to purchase both Addison Rae skins, along with associated accessories, going for the Addison Rae Bundle worth 3,600 V-Bucks would be economical. It provides you with all the Addison Rae items available in Fortnite’s Item Shop at a discount of 4,000 V-Bucks.

All Addison Rae cosmetics in Fortnite

1. Addison’s Sundae (back bling)

Price: 400 V-Bucks
Also available with: Addison Rae Bundle

2. Aquamarine the Turtle (back bling)

Price: 400 V-Bucks
Also available with: Addison Rae skin, Addison Rae Bundle

3. Fame Scepter (pickaxe)

Price: 800 V-Bucks
Also available with: Addison Rae Bundle

4. Addison’s Biggest Fan (pickaxe)

Price: 800 V-Bucks
Also available with: Famous Addison Rae skin, Addison Rae Bundle

5. Addison’s Mic (pickaxe and back bling)

Price: 800 V-Bucks
Also available with: Addison Rae Bundle

6. Addison (wrap)

Price: 300 V-Bucks
Also available with: Addison Rae Bundle

7. It’s Addison (loading screen)

Exclusively available with: Addison Rae Bundle

8. Diet Pepsi (emote)

Price: 500 V-Bucks
Also available with: Addison Rae Bundle

9. Fame is a Gun (emote)

Price: 500 V-Bucks
Also available with: Addison Rae Bundle

10. Diet Pepsi (jam track)

Price: 500 V-Bucks
Also available with: Addison Rae Bundle

11. Fame is a Gun (jam track)

Price: 500 V-Bucks
Also available with: Addison Rae Bundle

Wrapping up

Addison Rae is the newest in a series of singers who have been featured in Fortnite so far in 2026. Earlier, her contemporaries included Olivia Rodrigo, Chappell Roan, Laufey, and Lisa, among others. Most recently, Lil Tecca was brought to the Item Shop, being the headline artist for the Fortnite Festival season that kicked off on July 30, 2026.

The consistency with which in-game cosmetics based on music industry figures have rolled out over the past several months has made it understandably an exciting time for the concerned section of Fortnite fans. Interestingly, going by the comments on Fortnite’s X posts announcing Addison Rae, it appears that among the most-wanted artists for the game’s next music collab are Madison Beer and Charli XCX.

In case you missed:

  • How to get the Yoruichi Bleach Wave 2 skin in Fortnite
  • How to get Spider-Man Brand New Day skins in Fortnite
  • How to get John Wick’s dog in Fortnite
  • How to get Stranger Things skins in Fortnite

title.rendered: The Windows Clipboard shortcut I wish I started using years ago

content.rendered:
I’ve lost count of how many times I’ve stared at text on my screen and thought, “Why can’t I just copy this?” It might have been text inside an image, a screenshot, a scanned PDF, a paused video, an error message, or a website that simply wouldn’t let me select and copy something.

So I did what most people do: I typed it. Sometimes it was just a sentence, a long error message, or a URL with enough random characters to make typing it manually frustrating. But not anymore, as Windows can now extract text from the screen with just a keyboard shortcut.

Here’s how to use the hidden Windows shortcut for faster copying.

Windows 11 now offers Text Actions as a shortcut

For a feature this useful, Windows hides it surprisingly well. I accidentally stumbled upon a new text-extraction feature in the Snipping Tool. It uses OCR (optical character recognition) to find text inside a screen capture and turn it into something you can copy and paste.

Microsoft says you can use Text Actions to extract text from an image, copy everything in the selected area of the screen, and even quickly redact things like email addresses and phone numbers. The interesting part is that you can access the tool only by pressing the Win + Shift + T shortcut.

Therefore, I don’t need the original text to be selectable. If it’s visible, Windows can try to read it. That makes the shortcut useful for copying text from:

  • Images and screenshots
  • Scanned documents and PDFs
  • Video frames
  • Error messages
  • Photos
  • Presentation slides
  • Infographics
  • Apps that don’t allow normal text selection
  • Web pages where copying text isn’t straightforward

I don’t use Win + Shift + T instead of traditional Ctrl + C and Ctrl + V. I use it when normal copy and paste fails me. That’s why it has become one of my favorite Windows shortcuts.

Before Win + Shift + T, I used to do this

I used to have a complicated process for copying text that wasn’t selectable. If the text was in an image, I’d sometimes search for the original image or website, pause the video to type what was on the screen, or manually type the error message into Google.

And if the text was particularly annoying, I’d take a screenshot and then open it in another app to extract the text. These little interruptions add up to tank my productivity.

The worst one was probably the error messages. You know the ones: a long string of technical text that you want to search online. The message is sitting right there on the screen, but you can’t select it. So you start typing. One wrong character later, your Google search is useless.

With Win + Shift + T, that’s usually no longer necessary. I can select the error message, copy the extracted text, paste it into a search engine, and get back to the actual task. It sounds like a tiny improvement, but it’s worth knowing to save time and effort.

How to copy text from your screen

Using the Windows text extractor is remarkably simple.

  1. Press the Windows key + Shift + T at the same time. Windows opens the text extraction interface.
  2. Click and drag around the area containing the text you want to copy. I’ve found that selecting a too-small area doesn’t trigger extraction.
  3. Windows uses OCR to recognize the characters inside your selection.
  4. Once Windows has recognized the text, you may adjust the selection.
  5. Click the three-dot icon and select Remove line breaks to avoid copying the breaks.
  6. Now, click Copy all text at the top.
  7. Use Ctrl + V to paste the extracted text into a document, search box, email, note, chat, or wherever else you need it. It will appear as plain text without any formatting.

That’s it. The entire process takes only a few seconds and successfully recognizes custom fonts and text on difficult backgrounds.

Tip: As I use the feature all the time, I have enabled automatic copying. After pressing the shortcut, click the three-dot icon on the toolbar and select Automatically copy text.

The situations where I use this Windows OCR shortcut now

The interesting thing about Win + Shift + T is that I didn’t immediately start using it everywhere. It gradually replaced all those browser extensions, PowerToys, and online OCR services.

Here are the situations where it has become part of my regular workflow:

Troubleshooting a PC

This is probably one of the most useful situations. When troubleshooting Windows, you may come across error messages, warning dialogs, installation screens, software license keys, command output, or technical information that you need to search for online.

Instead of typing a long string character by character, I resort to the OCR shortcut to pull the text right off my screen and paste it into a search engine, a support forum, or a chat with someone helping me troubleshoot the problem.

Office work

OCR also comes in handy during everyday Office work. Sometimes the information I need is sitting inside reports, charts, slide decks, or scanned contracts rather than in an editable format.

For example, if someone sends you a screenshot containing a few figures, a reference number, or a paragraph that you need in Word or Excel, you can select the text directly instead of retyping it.

This is especially useful for small pieces of information. The shortcut lets me handle that small task quickly without turning it into a separate document-conversion project.

Studying and research

During research, I often come across useful text that appears in a format where standard text selection doesn’t work. It could be a screenshot from an online lecture, an eBook, a diagram with labels, a PDF handout, a scanned page, or an image containing a definition or quotation.

The OCR shortcut gives me a quick way to pull that information into my notes. I can select the relevant section, copy the extracted text, and put it alongside my other study material.

Everyday tasks

There are plenty of small, unremarkable situations where the shortcut is useful too.

Maybe I have a tracking number in a screenshot, a phone number displayed in an image, an address on a digital flyer, recipe ingredients from a cooking video, or some text in a photo that I want to search or send to someone. These aren’t tasks that justify installing a dedicated OCR app or PDF editor, or setting up a complicated workflow.

In such cases, simply use the shortcut, select the text, and move on.

Working with archived documents

Older documents are often stored as scans or images, which means the text may not be selectable even though it is perfectly readable.

When I need a particular name, date, reference number, or passage from one of these documents, there is no need to convert the entire archive into searchable PDFs. Just use the OCR shortcut on the relevant page and extract the required section.

When I don’t want to install another tool

Another practical advantage is that you can use the OCR capability as part of your existing Windows workflow rather than reaching for a separate OCR website or application.

For a one-off extraction, opening another service feels daunting. It requires you to upload the image, wait for it to process, copy the result, and potentially deal with formatting. With the shortcut, the text is already on my screen, so I can work with it immediately.

What I like about Windows’ text extraction

  • It is already there: There’s nothing new to install just to extract a few words from a screenshot. The feature is built into the Snipping Tool on supported versions of Windows 11.
  • Faster than finding the original source: When working with text inside an image, I ask myself whether I actually need the original webpage to get all the information. If you only need the text, extracting it is often faster.
  • It changed what I consider “copyable”: This is probably the biggest difference. We all think that only the text highlighted by the mouse pointer is copyable. Now my definition is that I can extract any text on the screen.

Limitations you should know about

I don’t want to oversell this. Win + Shift + T is useful, but it isn’t magic.

It uses OCR, and the recognizer can make mistakes. If the text is blurry, tiny, distorted, heavily stylized, or set against a complex background, the extracted result might need some cleanup.

I’ve also learned not to blindly trust extracted text when accuracy really matters.

For example, you should always double-check:

  • URLs
  • Email addresses
  • Code
  • Product or serial numbers
  • Technical terms
  • Numbers
  • Long strings of characters

One wrong character can completely change the meaning.

Moreover, it works with rectangular selections, so you can’t precisely outline text while excluding nearby icons, graphics, or other on-screen elements. If those elements are close to the text you’re trying to capture, the OCR may pick up extra characters or information.

In such instances, the simplest way out is to modify the selection and attempt it once more. If the unwanted text is only a few characters, I simply remove them after pasting the result into a document. It’s a small extra step, but still quicker than typing the entire selection manually.

Other Windows Clipboard shortcuts I use daily

Once I started paying more attention to Windows keyboard shortcuts, I realized that Win + Shift + T isn’t the only one that makes working with text easier.

These are the ones I use most.

  • Ctrl + C — Copy: The classic. Select something and press Ctrl + C to copy it. I still use this far more often than Win + Shift + T. The difference is that Ctrl + C requires selectable content.
  • Ctrl + V — Paste: Still indispensable. Once I’ve extracted text, Ctrl + V is usually how I get it where it needs to go.
  • Win + V — Clipboard History: It opens the Windows Clipboard History, letting you access items you’ve recently copied instead of being limited to just what you copied last. To enable it, go to Settings > System > Clipboard and toggle on Clipboard history. You can also sync your clipboard with other devices for continuity.
  • Win + Shift + S — Snipping Tool: I use Win + Shift + S when I actually want a screenshot or screen recording. The toolbar also offers a Quick markup tool to annotate screenshots and a Color picker tool to copy the color value from your screen.

Grab text from your screen quickly!

The Windows OCR shortcut is a small feature that can make everyday work noticeably easier. Whether I’m copying text, grabbing information from screenshots, or switching between different pieces of content, it saves time and reduces unnecessary retyping.

It’s simple, practical, and easy to build into your routine. I just wish I’d started using it years ago. And if you’re using Windows 11 and you’ve never tried Win + Shift + T, I’d suggest pressing it the next time you see text you can’t copy.

You might end up wondering, as I did: Why was I typing all of this myself?

  • 5 tips that improved my Windows search

mainEntity.name: Which cosmetics do I get after purchasing Phantom Blade Zero on the Epic Games Store?

acceptedAnswer.text: Upon purchasing Phantom Blade Zero via the store, you will automatically unlock the Soul outfit, the Sanguine pickaxe, and the Sanguine back bling.

mainEntity.name: Which platforms will the Phantom Blade Zero cosmetics be available on?

acceptedAnswer.text: As long as you are using the same Epic Games Store account that you used to pre-order the game, you will be able to use the skin across all platforms where Fortnite is available.

acceptedAnswer.text: The Soul outfit can be claimed in Fortnite as a freebie with Phantom Blade Zero's purchase as long as the latter game is still available on the PC storefront. Hence, it can be interpreted as a permanent offer.

title.rendered: Fortnite x Sonic the Hedgehog crossover confirmed for Chapter 7 Season 4

content.rendered:
After weeks of anticipation and leaks, the Fortnite x Sonic The Hedgehog collab for Fortnite’s Chapter 7 Season 4 has been confirmed via the latter franchise’s official social media accounts. The forthcoming season, titled Fortnite Override, is scheduled to roll out on August 20, 2026.

For a considerable time, video game collabs have been expected to feature heavily in the new Fortnite season. With the official tease coming from Sega, at least one such partnership has now been set in stone. Apart from fresh gaming content coming to Fortnite, hacking has also been expected to arrive and play a key role after the mid-month update.

Fortnite x Sonic The Hedgehog: Teaser breakdown

On August 10, Sega uploaded a teaser video that gave fans a glimpse of Sonic in a map location inspired by Green Hill. The clip shows the blue hedgehog sprinting on a hooped track, collecting the iconic gold rings synonymous with the long-running Sega-owned franchise.

There is also a shot of Fortnite character Peely sprinting similarly, which could be a hint at a Sonic The Hedgehog-themed item that grants super speed. Further, certain eagle-eyed fans also spotted how the clouds shown in the video resemble Tetris blocks, adding to the speculation of a collab with the namesake game franchise.

Notably, the first few seconds of the clip show a terminal screen with a cascade of commands. This, coupled with the title of the video, which says “HACKING Now”, is yet another strong indicator of hacking being incorporated as an aspect of Fortnite Override. On the online game’s Discord, an entire channel is dedicated to something called “Lobby Hack codes”, the purpose of which should become clearer when the forthcoming update drops.

All rumored content in Fortnite x Sonic The Hedgehog

Over the past few weeks, a bunch of Fortnite game collabs were reported to be in the pipeline. Given that Fortnite Override is shaping up as a season that significantly focuses on video game characters and locations, it is reasonable to think these leaked partnerships are slated to release as part of the new seasonal content. The following games and items are among those expected to land, per popular leakers such as Shiina, HYPEX, and FireMonkey.

1. Sonic The Hedgehog skin

SONIC SKIN IS COMING NEXT SEASON

SEGA → “HACKING Now: Sonic In For..t… Sonic, have you heard of a ‘Fortnite’?”

[Noticed by @Loolo_WRLD] pic.twitter.com/cSdGf2hEso

— HYPEX (@HYPEX) August 10, 2026

2. Tetris clouds in map

CLOUDS NEXT SEASON WILL BE TETRIS SHAPED pic.twitter.com/ZZGBivE3aF

— HYPEX (@HYPEX) August 10, 2026

3. Minecraft collab

MINECRAFT x FORTNITE SEEMS TO BE COMING IN C7S4

"SurviveTheNight" was NOT for FNAF, as @Minecraft have the exact same slogan in their bio & Adira mentioned this collab earlier this year.. pic.twitter.com/9uSsYCZvN9

— HYPEX (@HYPEX) August 10, 2026

4. Persona collab

FORTNITE X PERSONA – OFFICIALLY CONFIRMED

"Take Your Heart" is a hidden teaser in Fortnite's Discord bot pic.twitter.com/r9gSRvIjWt

— Shiina (@ShiinaBR) August 10, 2026

5. More Gaming Legends series collabs

FORTNITE SEASON 4 – GAMING LEGENDS

– Sonic
– Eggman
– Persona
– Megaman
– Tetris
– Pac-Man
– And even more!!

(Confirmed by me & @HYPEX with encrypted files) pic.twitter.com/pFzDyL9699

— Shiina (@ShiinaBR) July 30, 2026

Fortnite Override will also retain a fan-favorite feature

While the gaming-themed updates and additions in Fortnite Override certainly offer something to be excited about for Fortnite fans, that is not where the stream of new content ends. More specifically, it has been confirmed by Epic Games that Fortnite Chapter 7 Season 4 will also feature its own set of sprites.

However, that doesn’t mean you will be able to use your existing collection of sprites for playing matches in the next season. That’s because those will be restricted to a new island called Sprite Garden, preventing them from being used in other modes such as Battle Royale. Instead, you will be able to catch new sprites and use them in Fortnite Override.

Given the sheer variety of sprites in Fortnite’s ongoing season, the forthcoming one undoubtedly offers great promise. While fan-made sprites such as the ammunition-granting Bullet Sprite have already been confirmed to launch next season, others made by Fortnite devs can be expected to refresh the lineup throughout the season, similar to how it is right now.

FAQs

How many game franchises could appear in Fortnite Override?

At least six different game franchises have been leaked by reliable insiders for the new Fortnite season. According to Shiina, this number could very well be exceeded.

How are sprites changing in Fortnite Override?

title.rendered: Apple Pay may finally launch in India this October

content.rendered:
Apple Pay could finally make its debut in India by late September or October 2026, nearly a decade after Apple first indicated plans to bring its digital payments service to the country. However, the reported launch is expected to initially focus on credit cards rather than India’s dominant Unified Payments Interface (UPI) network.

According to a Business Standard report, Apple is preparing to introduce Apple Pay with support for cards issued on global payment networks such as Visa and Mastercard. The service would allow eligible users to add supported cards to Apple Wallet and make contactless payments using an iPhone or Apple Watch at NFC-enabled point-of-sale terminals.

Apple Pay India launch may not include UPI

As we covered in an earlier report, one of the biggest limitations at launch could be the absence of UPI support.

Apple would reportedly need approval from the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) and a partnership with a sponsor bank to enable UPI transactions through Apple Pay. As a result, the initial rollout is expected to focus primarily on card-based payments.

This could make Apple Pay particularly appealing to India’s premium credit card users, especially those already using iPhones and Apple Watches for everyday tasks. However, the lack of UPI integration could limit its broader appeal among consumers who rely heavily on UPI apps for daily payments.

Banks seek lower fees ahead of Apple Pay launch

Apple is also reportedly negotiating transaction economics with major Indian card issuers ahead of the potential launch.

Sources cited by Business Standard claim Apple has been seeking around 15 to 20 basis points from the interchange fee generated on each credit card transaction. Some banks, however, are reportedly pushing for a lower rate of approximately 10 basis points.

The fee would reportedly be paid by card-issuing banks rather than being charged directly to customers or merchants.

Despite those negotiations, Apple Pay’s arrival could give India’s credit card ecosystem another growth catalyst. Pine Labs CEO Amrish Rau has said he expects Apple Pay to enter India before the end of 2026 and suggested that offering consumers a broader range of payment options could help drive further growth in credit card transactions.

Apple’s RBI compliance could pave the way for Apple Pay

The potential Apple Pay launch comes as Apple strengthens its payments and services presence in the Indian market.

In July, the company reportedly restored credit and debit card payment options for Indian users purchasing apps, subscriptions, and services such as iCloud. Apple had removed card-based payments several years earlier following changes to India’s recurring payment regulations.

The restoration followed Apple’s implementation of India’s card tokenization requirements. Under the regulatory framework, businesses cannot retain customers’ actual card numbers for recurring transactions. Instead, payments rely on unique tokens generated by authorized card networks.

Tokenized payment information must also comply with India’s local data storage requirements, helping Apple align its payment infrastructure with regulations set by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI).

A long-awaited payment option may finally reach India

Apple Pay’s reported India launch could therefore mark another significant step in Apple’s efforts to expand its payments ecosystem in one of the world’s fastest-growing digital payments markets.

Apple Pay is already available across more than 90 markets globally, making India a notable omission given the country’s growing iPhone user base and rapidly expanding digital payments ecosystem.

However, Apple has not officially confirmed the India launch timeline, participating banks, supported cards, or whether UPI integration will eventually follow. Those details could still change before the service becomes available.

Would you use Apple Pay for payments in India even if it launches without UPI support? Let us know in the comments below.

mainEntity.name: Which cosmetics do I get after purchasing Phantom Blade Zero on the Epic Games Store?

acceptedAnswer.text: Upon purchasing Phantom Blade Zero via the store, you will automatically unlock the Soul outfit, the Sanguine pickaxe, and the Sanguine back bling.

mainEntity.name: Which platforms will the Phantom Blade Zero cosmetics be available on?

acceptedAnswer.text: As long as you are using the same Epic Games Store account that you used to pre-order the game, you will be able to use the skin across all platforms where Fortnite is available.

mainEntity.name: Until when is the Phantom Blade Zero skin available with the game's purchase on the Epic Games Store?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Soul outfit can be claimed in Fortnite as a freebie with Phantom Blade Zero's purchase as long as the latter game is still available on the PC storefront. Hence, it can be interpreted as a permanent offer.

title.rendered: iOS 27 Lock Screen features: Everything new and how to use it

content.rendered:
The Lock Screen got its big redesign back in iOS 16, and since then, Apple has mostly left it alone. iOS 27 changes that. This year’s update brings a smaller movable clock, AI-generated wallpapers, a fix for photos that never fit the screen, and, finally, a way to dismiss that stubborn Now Playing widget. iOS 27 is in beta right now and releases publicly in September 2026.

Shrink the clock and move it out of the way

The Lock Screen clock has always sat large and centered, right where the best part of your wallpaper usually is. iOS 27 adds a compact mode that shrinks the clock and tucks it up next to the date, leaving your wallpaper almost completely uncovered.

  1. Touch and hold the Lock Screen, then tap Customize.
  2. Tap the clock to open the Font & Color panel.
  3. Tap the two horizontal bars icon in the top-right corner of the panel.
  4. Tap anywhere on the wallpaper, then tap Done.

The clock instantly shrinks and moves to the top row. You can still change its font, weight, and color in compact mode, though the Liquid Glass slider for the clock isn’t available while it’s compact. The setting applies per wallpaper, so you can keep a big clock on one Lock Screen and a compact one on another. Tap the same icon again to go back to the full-size clock.

Generate wallpapers with Image Playground

Instead of hunting for the perfect wallpaper, you can now describe one and let your iPhone make it. iOS 27 builds Image Playground directly into the wallpaper picker, so you don’t need to create an image elsewhere and set it manually.

  1. Go to Settings → Wallpaper → Add New Wallpaper. You can also long-press the Lock Screen and tap the + button.
  2. Tap Image Playground.
  3. Describe the wallpaper you want, or pick a photo from your library and apply a style like Retro Illustration or Animation.
  4. Set the result as your Lock Screen.

This needs Apple Intelligence, so it works on iPhone 15 Pro and later, including all iPhone 16 and 17 models. The results have the usual Image Playground look, stylized and illustration-like rather than photorealistic, so it’s better for fun, personalized wallpapers than realistic scenery.

Extend a photo that doesn’t fit the screen

Everyone has a favorite photo that falls apart as a wallpaper because it’s cropped too tight or shot in the wrong orientation. The new Extend option uses Apple Intelligence to generate matching detail around the edges of the photo, so it fills the entire screen naturally instead of getting zoomed and cropped.

  1. Go to Settings → Wallpaper → Add New Wallpaper and choose your photo.
  2. Tap the three-dot button.
  3. Tap Extend Wallpaper, then confirm with Extend.

It can also straighten a tilted horizon or add breathing room around a subject that’s too close to the frame. It won’t work on every image, and since the fill is AI-generated, simple backgrounds like skies and landscapes blend better than busy, detailed ones. There’s also a daily limit on how many images you can extend, though Apple hasn’t said the exact number.

Swipe away the Now Playing widget

Until now, once you played music or a video, the Now Playing widget parked itself on your Lock Screen until you were done. In iOS 27, you can finally clear it: swipe left across the playback controls, and a Clear button slides in. Tap it, and the widget disappears without stopping your audio.

Dismissing it also removes the Now Playing bubble from the Dynamic Island, so your music keeps playing in the background with a completely clean screen. The widget comes back if you pause and resume playback, and it’s per app, so starting media in a different app brings up a fresh widget.

Adjust how transparent Liquid Glass looks

If you found Liquid Glass too see-through in iOS 26, or you actually liked the clear look and wanted more of it, iOS 27 gives you a full slider instead of the old two-position toggle.

  1. Open Settings and tap Appearance.
  2. Tap Liquid Glass.
  3. Drag the slider left for a clearer, more transparent look, or right for a more tinted, solid one.

The change applies system-wide, and on the Lock Screen, it affects the clock, widgets, and notifications, so text stays readable even on busy wallpapers if you push the slider toward tinted. Appearance is a new Settings section in iOS 27 that also holds Light/Dark mode and text size. If the slider still isn’t enough, Reduce Transparency under Settings → Accessibility → Display & Text Size removes nearly all translucency.

None of these are headline features on their own, but together they fix most of the long-standing Lock Screen complaints: the clock covering wallpapers, photos that don’t fit, and the Now Playing widget that wouldn’t leave. If you’re on the iOS 27 beta, the compact clock and Extend are the two worth trying first. Everyone else gets them in September; until then, there’s still plenty you can customize on your Lock Screen in iOS 26.

Make your iPhone Lock Screen your own

iOS 27 may not completely reinvent the Lock Screen, but these small changes make it noticeably more useful and personal. The compact clock gives your wallpaper more room to shine, Image Playground lets you create custom backgrounds, and Extend finally fixes those photos that never quite fit the screen.

I also appreciate the ability to dismiss the Now Playing widget without stopping playback, while the new Liquid Glass controls give you more freedom to fine-tune how the interface looks.

If you’re already running the iOS 27 beta, I’d recommend trying the compact clock and Extend feature first. For everyone else, these changes will arrive with the public release in September 2026—and they make the Lock Screen worth customizing all over again.

mainEntity.name: Which cosmetics do I get after purchasing Phantom Blade Zero on the Epic Games Store?

acceptedAnswer.text: Upon purchasing Phantom Blade Zero via the store, you will automatically unlock the Soul outfit, the Sanguine pickaxe, and the Sanguine back bling.

mainEntity.name: Which platforms will the Phantom Blade Zero cosmetics be available on?

acceptedAnswer.text: As long as you are using the same Epic Games Store account that you used to pre-order the game, you will be able to use the skin across all platforms where Fortnite is available.

mainEntity.name: Until when is the Phantom Blade Zero skin available with the game's purchase on the Epic Games Store?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Soul outfit can be claimed in Fortnite as a freebie with Phantom Blade Zero's purchase as long as the latter game is still available on the PC storefront. Hence, it can be interpreted as a permanent offer.

mainEntity.name: Until when is the Phantom Blade Zero skin available with the game's purchase on the Epic Games Store?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Soul outfit can be claimed in Fortnite as a freebie with Phantom Blade Zero's purchase as long as the latter game is still available on the PC storefront. Hence, it can be interpreted as a permanent offer.

mainEntity.name: Is it legal to download videos from X (Formerly Twitter)?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, you can download videos for watching later or for other personal use. But reposting, especially for commercial use, may violate copyright laws. Always credit the original creator and seek permission before reuploading.

mainEntity.name: How to download a private Twitter video?

acceptedAnswer.text: For a private or protected X account, the only way is to screen record the video. Most third-party X video downloaders support only public posts. I wouldn't recommend trying to bypass the account's privacy controls.

acceptedAnswer.text: The last live event was called Shattered, and it took place on June 5, 2026. It bridged the gap between Chapter 7 Season 2 and Season 3.

title.rendered: iOS 27 beta 5 brings new app icons, British Siri voices, and better Search settings

content.rendered:
Apple released iOS 27 developer beta 5 on Monday, and it reads like a final polish pass before next month’s launch. The update swaps in redesigned app icons, expands Siri AI’s voice customization to British English, and adds a new Search settings section, according to 9to5Mac’s beta 5 roundup.

There’s no single headline feature here. Instead, Apple is tightening up Liquid Glass, trimming clutter from Control Center, and settling small details across Settings, Contacts, and Wallet.

Redesigned icons for Safari, Siri, and more

Beta 5 refreshes the Liquid Glass icons for Safari, Siri, Settings, Remote, Preview, and the App Store. Safari’s icon now has a small dot at its center, while Siri’s leans harder into the glassy look. Apple also toned down the saturation of the Siri animation, so invoking the assistant feels a little calmer.

A few apps, including Photos, Wallet, Music, and the App Store, picked up new launch screens too.

Siri AI voices now speak British English

Siri AI’s voice customization first appeared in beta 3 with American English only. Beta 5 extends the Pace and Expressivity sliders to all seven American voices and four British voices, so UK users can finally tune how the new assistant sounds.

The catch hasn’t changed: Siri AI still requires an iPhone 17 Pro, iPhone 17 Pro Max, or iPhone Air, since the rebuilt assistant needs 12GB of RAM to run on device. Even on a supported iPhone, Siri AI won’t show up until you enable it and clear the waitlist.

A new “Before Searching” section in Settings

Search settings gain a Before Searching section that controls what shows up before you type. You can set app suggestions to off, four, or eight results, and toggle shortcuts and recent searches. There’s also a new Search the Web option in the results.

It’s a small change, but it gives you real control over a screen that used to be take-it-or-leave-it.

The smaller changes worth knowing

Beyond the headline tweaks, beta 5 quietly cleans up several everyday screens:

  • Control Center no longer shows your cellular network type (5G or LTE) while you’re on Wi-Fi.
  • Contacts displays company names under people’s names in lists and search results.
  • Wallet’s Create a Pass feature now works outside the US, MacRumors found.
  • Software Update shows when you last installed an update.
  • Battery settings can warn you when a weak cellular signal is draining your battery.
  • Mail adds a Personalize Smart Replies toggle, off by default.
  • The 5G+ indicator expands to EE in the UK and carriers in Spain.

What comes next

This build will likely roll out to public beta testers as iOS 27 public beta 3 in the coming days. The final release is expected in September alongside the new iPhone lineup, so the remaining betas should keep the bug-fix focus that started with beta 4’s Camera, Siri, and CarPlay fixes.

iOS 27 runs on the iPhone 11 and later, plus the iPhone SE 2 and newer, though Siri AI and the wider Apple Intelligence features need recent hardware. If you don’t mind beta bugs, you can install the iOS 27 developer beta on a compatible iPhone right now.

mainEntity.name: Which cosmetics do I get after purchasing Phantom Blade Zero on the Epic Games Store?

acceptedAnswer.text: Upon purchasing Phantom Blade Zero via the store, you will automatically unlock the Soul outfit, the Sanguine pickaxe, and the Sanguine back bling.

mainEntity.name: Which platforms will the Phantom Blade Zero cosmetics be available on?

acceptedAnswer.text: As long as you are using the same Epic Games Store account that you used to pre-order the game, you will be able to use the skin across all platforms where Fortnite is available.

mainEntity.name: Until when is the Phantom Blade Zero skin available with the game's purchase on the Epic Games Store?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Soul outfit can be claimed in Fortnite as a freebie with Phantom Blade Zero's purchase as long as the latter game is still available on the PC storefront. Hence, it can be interpreted as a permanent offer.

title.rendered: Gurman: Apple’s Glass-Centric 20th Anniversary iPhone Is Still on Track for 2027

content.rendered:
Apple has not cancelled its big glass-heavy iPhone redesign. According to Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman, the glass-centric overhaul planned for the iPhone’s 20th anniversary is still coming in 2027, and Apple’s product roadmap hasn’t changed. The report lands a day after an analyst claimed the project was dead.

What the 2027 iPhone Pro will reportedly look like

Gurman says Apple expects to launch iPhone Pro models next year with a new glassy look. The phones, known internally as V73 and V74, use glass on the front and back, and the material curves into the sides of the device with a metal band running through the middle.

That is not the same thing as a true all-glass iPhone, and that distinction seems to be the source of the confusion. Gurman notes Apple did explore a more ambitious version that used even more glass instead of metal, but it was scrapped early in development. Joining the glass panels together proved difficult, and the design couldn’t be produced reliably at scale.

The cancellation claim came from Jefferies

A day earlier, Jefferies analyst Edison Lee said his firm’s supply-chain checks showed the all-glass anniversary iPhone had been cancelled over poor production yields. Jefferies downgraded Apple to Underperform and cut its price target to $263.66, arguing the cancellation weakens Apple’s ability to push iPhone prices higher. Lee had estimated the all-glass model would have sold at a blended price of around $2,060.

Read next to Gurman’s report, the most likely explanation is that Jefferies picked up the death of the abandoned all-glass prototype, not the phone Apple actually plans to ship. The glass-and-metal-band design is reportedly moving ahead as planned.

Why 2027 is the year to watch

The iPhone turns 20 in 2027, and rumors of a special anniversary redesign have been building since 2025. Gurman had already described a mostly glass, curved iPhone as the centerpiece of Apple’s 2027 plans, alongside foldables and new AI hardware. A curved-glass iPhone Pro would be the biggest visual change to the lineup in years, and it fits Apple’s long-running goal of a phone that looks like a single slab of glass.

The redesign also arrives as Apple reshuffles its release calendar. Ming-Chi Kuo expects Apple to split its iPhone launches into two waves, with Pro models in the fall and standard models the following spring, and the first foldable iPhone is expected to debut in 2026 before the anniversary model lands.

As always with reports this far out, details can shift before launch. But for now, the redesign everyone assumed was dead appears to be very much alive.

title.rendered: ChatGPT can now book restaurant tables and join waitlists through Yelp

content.rendered:
You no longer have to leave ChatGPT to lock in a dinner reservation. Yelp announced that its Reservations and Waitlist features now work directly inside ChatGPT, so you can book a table or join the queue at thousands of restaurants across the US and Canada without switching apps.

The whole flow happens in one conversation. Ask ChatGPT for restaurant suggestions, and it pulls up Yelp-powered results with reviews, ratings, and photos. Pick a place, and you can set the party size, date, time, contact details, and any special requests right in the chat, then get your confirmation. If the restaurant is full, you can join its waitlist instead.

One thing still lives outside the chat: changing your plans. Once a booking is made, you manage or modify the reservation through Yelp, not ChatGPT.

ChatGPT now covers all three big booking services

Yelp is not the only reservation option in ChatGPT. The official ChatGPT account confirmed on X that you can find and book a table through OpenTable, Resy, or Yelp directly in a conversation. OpenTable bookings work globally, Resy covers the US, and Yelp handles the US and Canada.

That lineup matters if you actually eat out. Between the three services, most bookable restaurants in North America are now reachable from a single ChatGPT conversation, which used to end with “here are five suggestions, good luck.”

It also fits OpenAI’s bigger push to make ChatGPT do things instead of just suggesting them, from the ChatGPT Work agent that handles multi-step tasks to the upcoming Apple Music integration that builds playlists right in the chat.

Built on the July partnership

Yelp and OpenAI started this in late July, when Yelp reviews, ratings, photos, and business details began showing up in ChatGPT answers for local searches. Booking is the obvious next step, and Yelp has a number to justify it: in a Morning Consult study it cites, 65% of people said being able to take action, like making a reservation, matters when they use AI tools for local discovery.

Restaurants get something out of this too. Bookings made in ChatGPT flow into Yelp Guest Manager, the same system restaurants already use to run their front of house, so a table booked in a chatbot shows up like any other reservation.

Neither company mentions any plan restrictions, so the feature does not appear to be locked behind a paid ChatGPT tier.

title.rendered: How to get Peely Sprite in Fortnite and what it does

content.rendered:
After bringing sprites inspired by third parties, such as the John Wick Sprite, Fortnite has recently looked inward once again and introduced the Peely Sprite to players. It is modeled around Peely, an iconic Fortnite skin that was first rolled out in 2019.

Apart from Peely Sprite, another new sprite that takes inspiration from an existing Fortnite skin is the Llama Sprite, which was dropped on the same day, July 30. Prior to these, the only other original character-based sprite in the game was the Duck Sprite, which was also among the earliest sprites released at the beginning of Fortnite Runners season.

What the Peely Sprite does in Fortnite

Peely Sprite offers a unique power to the players, using which they get a ping when there are other players with rare sprites nearby, but at the cost of marking their own position on the map. This ability can prove useful when hunting for some of the most coveted Mythic-tier sprites, such as the Pollo Sprite. In other words, getting your hands on the Peely Sprite makes it easier to locate and nab other sought-after sprites.

Moreover, the Peely Sprite is also available in five different variants, including the base variant. The other forms of this sprite include its Gold, Gummy, Holofoil, and Galaxy versions. As expected, the non-base variants offer additional perks on top of the Peely Sprite’s own ability.

Where to find Peely Sprite in Fortnite

Hunting for chests and breaking into vaults

Peely Sprite is a Legendary-tier item in Fortnite. This means that it is among the rarer sprites available in the battle royale game, making it highly unlikely to be found roaming around in the open. As such, your best bet is to obtain this critter from one of the chests scattered all over the map. In particular, sprite chests and other special chests have a relatively higher chance of spawning the Peely Sprite compared to ordinary chests.

Apart from open locations and accessible buildings, many rare sprites and the chests that offer them can also be found in hidden locations, such as vaults. These locked-away rooms can be accessed using a vault key, which is often placed somewhere in the vicinity of the vault room. So, when you find either one of these two things, you can readily know that the other must be somewhere close on the map.

Taking it from opponents

While chest-hunting and vault-ransacking are among the two most straightforward ways of catching the Peely Sprite. It can also be retrieved by eliminating someone who already extracted the sprite before.

To do this, you need to have a player equipped with the Peely Sprite join the same Fortnite match as yours. While the chances of this happening can’t exactly be predicted, it is still best to be prepared.

So, to pull this off, make sure to check the sprites players carry on their back while you are still at the Spawn Island and remember the appearance of the opponent who has a sprite you desire. When he jumps off from the Battle Bus, you must follow that player, track him down, and eliminate him to take his sprite and successfully extract the same.

Indexing from friendly players

On Fortnite’s official Discord, there is a channel by the name of “sprite-runners-network”. There, you can find players willing to help others complete their sprite collection using the indexing method. What this approach entails is joining a match with another player who has a sprite you want and then borrowing it from him for extraction. Later, in the next match, you can tag along with the same player and return the acquired sprite to its original owner.

At any time, you can easily get your hands on a previously extracted sprite from the Sprites tab in Fortnite. Importantly, doing this requires a certain amount of Sprite Dust and this amount increases based on how rare the sprite is.

Rounding up

For those hell-bent on adding to their sprite collection, Peely Sprite is certainly a useful item that pushes them towards that goal. If you are one of those players, you can equip this particular sprite whenever there are new ones introduced in the game, to boost your odds of acquiring them early.

Apart from the Peely Sprite, there is an entire variant that further amplifies the possibility of grabbing highly elusive sprites, known as holofoil sprites. Equipping any one sprite from this family of sprites adds a staggering 30% likelihood of obtaining sprites that are hard to find during a match.

You Might Also Like

  • What does the Punk Sprite do in Fortnite?

title.rendered: I switched between Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 and Apple Watch Ultra 3: Here’s the better buy

content.rendered:
Samsung has finally unveiled the latest addition to its Ultra lineup: the Galaxy Watch Ultra 2. After going through its specs, my first question was simple: Is it better than the Apple Watch Ultra 3?

Both watches promise flagship performance, advanced health tracking, rugged durability, and smarter AI-powered features. But specifications only tell part of the story.

Instead of relying solely on spec sheets and marketing claims, I switched between the Samsung Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 and Apple Watch Ultra 3 to see how they actually compare in everyday use. Surprisingly, the winner wasn’t as obvious as I expected.

If you’re trying to decide between these two flagship smartwatches, you’re in the right place. I’ll compare the Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 and Apple Watch Ultra 3 across design, display, performance, health tracking, battery life, smart features, and value to help you decide which one is right for you.

Samsung Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 vs Apple Watch Ultra 3: Quick specs comparison

On paper, both watches look incredibly close, but real-world use tells a different story.

Design and comfort: Rugged outside, premium on the wrist

The Samsung Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 and Apple Watch Ultra 3 are built for adventure, but they take very different approaches to design.

Samsung refines its signature look with the Galaxy Watch Ultra 2, continuing the iconic cushion design in a noticeably thinner profile. I like how the display and bezel flow together into a single, seamless form and give a clean, premium appearance. Crafted from Grade 4 titanium, it weighs only 61.5 g, making it comfortable for all-day wear despite its rugged build.

Samsung has also redesigned the buttons, making them more tactile and intuitive. I can now locate the Quick Button quickly even with gloves on.

Apple sticks to its instantly recognizable Ultra design. The Apple Watch Ultra 3 features a Grade 5 titanium frame that weighs 61.6 g. While it’s slightly larger than Samsung’s offering, it remains well-balanced on the wrist. The rectangular display, Digital Crown, and customizable Action Button prioritize usability, especially when navigating apps or checking notifications.

Despite their nearly identical weights, the two watches wear differently. The Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 offers a more classic watch experience with its circular appearance, whereas I personally favor the bolder, functional look of the Apple Watch Ultra 3.

My verdict: Pick the Samsung Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 for the timeless classic look. In case you need a bigger display and more user-friendly interactions on the screen, choose Apple Watch Ultra 3.

Display quality: Samsung wins on brightness, Apple wins on screen space

When I first started comparing the Samsung Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 and Apple Watch Ultra 3, I assumed the displays would be nearly identical. But once I got to use both, I saw some major differences.

The Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 immediately impressed me with its 1.52-inch Super AMOLED display. With a peak brightness of 5,000 nits, it was incredibly easy to read outdoors. Combined with its 498 × 498 resolution, everything from watch faces to workout metrics looked sharp and vibrant.

The Apple Watch Ultra 3, meanwhile, offers a larger 1.98-inch Retina LTPO3 OLED display with 3,000 nits of peak brightness. While it’s not as bright as Samsung’s on paper, I rarely found visibility to be an issue.

What I noticed more was the extra screen space. Long texts, Apple Maps navigation, or even viewing fitness data became a lot easier on the larger rectangular display and wide-angle OLED panel. Both watches use sapphire crystal glass, so I never worried about scratches during everyday use.

My Verdict: If I spent most of my time outdoors, I would definitely opt for the Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 as its display performs better in direct sunlight. But for everyday tasks, I liked the Apple Watch Ultra 3‘s larger screen better.

Performance and software: The real battle isn’t speed; it’s the ecosystem

In terms of performance, I expected a clear winner. Instead, what stood out was how both watches are already so fast that the hardware almost fades into the background.

The Samsung Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 runs Wear OS 7 with One UI Watch 9, powered by the Snapdragon SW6100 Wear Elite (3nm) chipset. It sports a penta-core CPU, which makes everything – from launching apps to switching between workouts – very smooth. The best part is I can customize watch faces, widgets, and quick settings more freely.

Samsung blends Google’s ecosystem with Samsung-exclusive features. That means you get native access to Google Maps, Google Wallet, Gmail, Google Calendar, and more. Moreover, Samsung Galaxy phone owners gain even deeper integration through Galaxy AI features, SmartThings controls, camera remote functions, and seamless device switching.

The Apple Watch Ultra 3 runs watchOS 26 (upgradable to watchOS 27) and is powered by Apple’s S10 chip with a dual-core CPU and PowerVR GPU. Animations are buttery smooth, apps open instantly, and navigating the interface feels effortless.

I prefer it thanks to its seamless integrations with the iPhone, which makes activities such as sending messages, locating the phone, unlocking the Mac, controlling my smart home, or even making payments using Apple Pay seem almost effortless.

My Verdict: If you’re an Android user, the Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 offers more customization and tight integration with Google’s ecosystem. As I am an iPhone user, Apple wins on software refinement and ecosystem integration.

Health and fitness tracking: Samsung packs in more features, Apple keeps it simple

Both Apple and Samsung have transformed their watches from simple notification devices into sophisticated health companions capable of tracking everything from heart rate and sleep to GPS workouts and recovery metrics.

The Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 is now equipped with AI health and fitness features intended to give us better personalized insights. The new Heart Health Score lets me get a simplified view of cardiovascular wellness, and Daily Cardio Load helps balance training and recovery. Fitness Index provides a broader view of physical fitness and supports personalized goals.

For outdoor athletes, Trail Run tracks elevation, climbing and terrain, while Nutrition Alert provides hydration guidance based on estimated sweat loss. The Ultra2 also introduces enhanced diving capabilities, tracking depth, dive time and water temperature, with an upcoming Mares-developed diving app adding more advanced metrics.

The Apple Watch Ultra 3 also stands out with advanced health monitoring and training tools. Its Hypertension Notifications can identify potential signs of chronic high blood pressure, while Sleep Score and sleep-apnea monitoring provide deeper insights into sleep quality and breathing disturbances.

For fitness, Ultra 3 offers Training Load, personalized Heart Rate Zones, Workout Buddy, and more. It also supports Power Zones for cycling, automatic swim-stroke detection, and multisport workout tracking. For adventurers, its full dive computer, Backtrack and built-in satellite communications add capabilities beyond conventional smartwatch fitness tracking.

My verdict: Choose Galaxy Watch Ultra2 for broader AI-powered health guidance, recovery and adventure features, whereas Apple Watch Ultra 3 is better for deeper workout analytics and a more established fitness ecosystem.

Battery life: Both keep up with you

If you want a smartwatch that can comfortably last through your day without constantly thinking about charging, the Galaxy Watch Ultra2 is the better fit.

Its 800mAh battery offers up to 60 hours with Always-On Display enabled. I went through long workouts, outdoor activities and overnight health tracking easily. Moreover, Samsung has included First Charging for the first time in a Galaxy Watch, providing up to 40% battery in just 30 minutes.

The Apple Watch Ultra 3 offers up to 42 hours of normal use and up to 72 hours in Low Power Mode. Its biggest advantage is charging speed, reaching up to 80% in around 45 minutes. I only charge for 15 minutes to get 12 hours of normal use.

Apple has claimed that the Watch Ultra 3 can go up to 14 hours of outdoor workout with full GPS and heart rate readings and up to 35 hours of outdoor workout with cellular in Low Power Mode with fewer GPS and heart rate readings.

My verdict: For longer, less interrupted use, I’d pick the Galaxy Watch Ultra2. If you value fast charging and flexible Low Power Mode, the Apple Watch Ultra 3 is more convenient.

Smart features and AI capabilities: Beyond fitness tracking

When choosing between the Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 and Apple Watch Ultra 3, my deciding factor came down to which one fits my daily routine.

Both watches allow me to make phone calls and send messages, pay for goods, stream music, navigate, get calendar notifications and weather alerts, and install third-party apps. The real difference is in ecosystem integration and AI assistant.

The Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 is the more flexible pick for Android users, particularly if you want AI to feel like a natural part of the watch. I only need to raise my wrist to activate Google Gemini to ask questions, set reminders, control tasks and get help without a wake word or button click. It also brings Google Play Store to explore countless apps for productivity.


Given that I’m an iPhone user, the Apple Watch Ultra 3 feels like a natural part of my phone’s experience. Features such as Apple Pay, Find My, Continuity features, Siri, and tight integration with Apple services create a seamless experience. Moreover, Apple Intelligence features like Workout Buddy and Live Translation make it more practical.

My verdict: Choose the Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 if you want conversational Gemini AI and the Google ecosystem. Go for the Apple Watch Ultra 3 if you already have an iPhone and want deeper ecosystem integration with personalized AI-powered fitness features.

Price & value: Which watch gives you more for your money?

The Galaxy Watch Ultra2 is the better value on price alone. Samsung lists it at $699.99, while the Apple Watch Ultra 3 starts at $799, putting the Galaxy ahead by $100.

That $100 difference matters if you have a Galaxy phone and want flagship features without stretching your budget. The Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 packs a titanium design, LTE, a 5,000-nit display, an 800mAh battery and up to 60 hours of usage with always-on display enabled.

The Apple Watch Ultra 3 justifies its higher price with features that will appeal particularly to iPhone users, including 5G, satellite connectivity, a titanium case, up to 42 hours of normal battery life and deeper integration with the Apple ecosystem.

Our pick for value: Galaxy Watch Ultra2. It gives switchers more hardware and battery for less money. But if you’re moving to an iPhone, the extra $100 for the Apple Watch Ultra 3 can be worthwhile because its biggest advantage is how seamlessly it works with the rest of Apple’s ecosystem.

Who should buy the Samsung Galaxy Watch Ultra 2?

Choose the Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 if you:

  • Use a Samsung Galaxy smartphone
  • Prefer Android and Google services
  • Want a traditional round watch design
  • Value customization
  • Want excellent battery life
  • Enjoy Samsung Health and body composition tracking

Who should buy the Apple Watch Ultra 3?

Choose the Apple Watch Ultra 3 if you:

  • Own an iPhone
  • Want the smoothest smartwatch experience available
  • Depend on Apple Health and Apple’s ecosystem
  • Prefer a large rectangular display for apps and notifications
  • Want Ultra Wideband support for Precision Finding
  • Require Satellite connectivity, especially Emergency SOS via satellite

Samsung Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 vs Apple Watch Ultra 3: Which premium smartwatch should you buy?

After comparing design, display, software, health tracking, battery life, and overall value, one conclusion stands out: There isn’t a single winner. There are two winners, each dominating its own ecosystem.

If you’re an iPhone user like me, the Apple Watch Ultra 3 is the obvious choice. It offers seamless integration, polished software, and an ecosystem that feels cohesive from your wrist to your phone. Pairing with the right accessories, this is my adventure companion.

On the other hand, if you’re an Android user, especially someone with a Samsung Galaxy device, the Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 is the smartwatch I’d recommend without hesitation. It combines rugged hardware, excellent battery life, deep Google integration, and meaningful health features into a package that feels purpose-built for Android.

The biggest mistake you can make is choosing a smartwatch based solely on a feature comparison chart. In daily use, the experience is shaped far more by how well the watch fits into your existing ecosystem.

title.rendered: WhatsApp is moving parental controls into the iPhone settings screen

content.rendered:
WhatsApp is adding a dedicated parental controls entry to its iOS settings, so parents can start a parent-managed account without digging for the option. WABetaInfo spotted the section in WhatsApp for iOS 26.30.77 on the App Store, and it is reaching accounts in stages rather than all at once.

Tapping it opens a guided setup instead of a settings list. The parent needs both phones in hand: they scan a QR code or accept an invite, then finish the rest on the child’s phone and enter the child’s date of birth. WhatsApp keeps that date private and uses it internally. According to the report, the controls come off on their own once the child turns 18, and the features that were held back unlock then.

The controls themselves are not new

WhatsApp launched parent-managed accounts on March 11, 2026, for pre-teens. The account is limited to messaging and calling, so Channels, Status, Meta AI, and disappearing messages in one-to-one chats are all off the table.

Parents decide who can contact the account and which groups it can join. Messages from unknown numbers go into a separate Requests inbox for the parent to approve or ignore, and the whole panel sits behind a parent PIN on the managed device.

None of that means reading the child’s chats. Messages on a managed account stay end-to-end encrypted, and what the parent sees is account-level activity: new contacts, blocks and reports, privacy setting changes, and group invites.

Android got the same treatment first

The Android app picked up a parental controls entry in its settings screen in late July. The reason WhatsApp is bothering with an entry point at all is adoption. The feature shipped in March, but parents had to already know it existed to find it, and plenty never did.

Putting it in Settings is a low-effort fix for that, and it lines the two apps up so a household with an iPhone and an Android phone follows the same instructions.

What to check on your iPhone

Update WhatsApp from the App Store first, then open Settings in the app and look for the parental controls entry. If it is not there yet, the rollout has not reached your account, and WhatsApp says it should widen over the coming weeks. Parent-managed accounts are also still rolling out by region, so the account type may not be live where you are.

The setup runs on the child’s phone as much as your own, so it is worth having both charged and unlocked before you start. Setting up a parent-managed WhatsApp account then comes down to approving contacts, handling group invites, and locking the privacy settings behind the PIN.

App-level controls like this are also filling gaps that Screen Time never covered, which is the same direction Apple is heading with iOS 27’s child safety changes.
